# Database reference

<!-- GENERATED by `make db-docs` from internal/platform/store/schemadoc/. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Every table and column Loomarr keeps, in plain words, grouped by the part of the app that uses
it. It's for anyone looking inside the database: to understand what Loomarr remembers, answer a
question the app doesn't show, or report a problem precisely.

## Looking without breaking anything

Look at a **copy**, never the live file. `make db-view` opens a copy of this database in a
browser-based viewer and deletes the copy when you stop it (see
[the dev loop](../contributing/dev-loop.md)). For a quick question about a SQLite install, a
read-only shell on a copy or a nightly backup works too:

```bash
sqlite3 -readonly loomarr-copy.db '.tables'
```

Don't change rows by hand. Loomarr checks what it writes, and a hand edit skips those checks.
Change things in the app, or open an issue if the app can't do what you need.

On Postgres, these descriptions are also stored as table and column comments, so most SQL
clients show them beside the data.

## Which table answers "what titles do we have"

`library_items`. A title is in the library when one of its `library_files` rows is present
(`missing_at_ms` is 0). The other title tables are layers around it, each with one job:

1. **`inventory_*`: what each importer reported.** One item per movie, show or episode, however
   many importers (a folder scan, an Emby or Jellyfin server) report it, with the files that play
   it. An item's id is fixed by its first report, so a title that comes back gets the same id.
2. **`library_*`: the answer.** One `library_items` row per title, with the same id as its
   inventory item, written in the same transaction as each inventory write, plus its details,
   files, artwork and collections. When the sources disagree, this is the one answer the app shows.
3. **`titles`: what channels asked for.** A movie or show a channel wants, tracked from wanted to
   available through Seerr or the arr apps. Once it arrives, `titles.library_id` says which item it
   became. Until the switch to Loomarr's own scanner (#2151) that is the media server's id, which
   the switch rewrites to the library's.

Every layer is pruned: the nightly housekeeping deletes reports, files and library rows long gone
(each table's retention says when).

## Which tables are growing

Every night, after its clean-up, the housekeeping task records how many rows each table holds in
`database_table_rows`, and keeps 400 days of counts. A table that keeps growing month after month
is one nothing trims. This lists the ten that grew most over the last 30 days, on SQLite or
Postgres:

```sql
SELECT latest.table_name, latest.row_count AS rows_now,
       latest.row_count - COALESCE(earlier.row_count, 0) AS grew_by
FROM database_table_rows latest
LEFT JOIN database_table_rows earlier
  ON earlier.table_name = latest.table_name
 AND earlier.recorded_at = latest.recorded_at - 30 * 86400
WHERE latest.recorded_at = (SELECT MAX(recorded_at) FROM database_table_rows)
ORDER BY grew_by DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

If Prometheus scrapes Loomarr, the latest counts are also the `loomarr_database_table_rows` gauge,
one series per table, so `delta(loomarr_database_table_rows[30d])` graphs the same growth.

## Reading the values

- **Times** are whole numbers counting from 1 January 1970 UTC. The name says the unit: a column
  ending in `_ms` counts milliseconds, `_ns` nanoseconds, and any other counts seconds. In SQLite,
  `datetime(col, 'unixepoch')` turns seconds into a date and `datetime(col / 1000, 'unixepoch')`
  does the same for milliseconds.
- **Yes/no** columns hold `1` for yes and `0` for no.
- Columns ending in **`_json`** hold a JSON document; their description says what's inside.
- **May be empty** in the Type column means the column can be `NULL`. A **key** column
  identifies the row. An arrow (→) names the table and column a value points at.
- Types are shown as SQLite declares them. Postgres uses its own equivalent for each.

## People and sign-in

Who can use Loomarr and how they prove it: accounts, browser sign-ins, paired TVs and phones, invitations, password recovery and email addresses, plus each person's own channel lists. Every secret here (passwords, sign-in cookies, device tokens, invitation and recovery links) is stored only as a one-way hash, which can't be turned back into a working credential.

### users

One row per person allowed into Loomarr. Rows are made by the first-admin setup, by an admin creating a local account, by importing a media-server account, or by someone redeeming an invitation. Accounts are never deleted; an admin disables them instead.

**Kept:** Kept forever: accounts are never deleted, only disabled.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the person. For a media-server account it is that server's user id; for a local account Loomarr makes one up. Other tables point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `name` | The person's name, which is also the username a local account signs in with. | `TEXT` |
| `role` | What the person may do. admin manages the household (people, settings, approvals); member watches and makes requests. | `TEXT` |
| `disabled` | 1 when an admin has turned the account off. A disabled person can't sign in, and their sign-ins and paired devices are deleted. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `quota` | How many of the person's approved requests may be waiting to arrive in the library at once. 0 means use the household default setting. | `INTEGER` |
| `auto_approve` | 1 when the person's requests skip the admin queue, as long as they stay within their quota. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `created_at` | When the account was made, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_at` | When the account was last changed, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `password_hash` | A one-way Argon2id hash of the local password, used only to check a password at sign-in; the password can't be recovered from it. Empty or NULL when the person has no local password. | `TEXT` · may be empty |
| `media_server_linked` | 1 when the account comes from the media server and signs in with that server's password, rather than being a Loomarr-only local account. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `last_seen_at` | When the person last used Loomarr from any sign-in or paired device, in Unix seconds, updated at most once a minute. 0 means not seen yet. | `BIGINT` |

### sessions

One row per browser sign-in. Made at sign-in or when an invitation is redeemed; deleted at sign-out, when an admin revokes it, when the password is reset or the account disabled, and by a regular sweep once it has expired.

**Kept:** Kept until sign-out, revocation or a password reset; the nightly housekeeping task deletes expired ones.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token_hash` | SHA-256 hash of the sign-in cookie. Only the browser holds the cookie itself; the hash can't be turned back into a working sign-in. | `TEXT` · key |
| `user_id` | The person signed in, from users. | `TEXT` · → `users.id` |
| `created_at` | When the person signed in, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `expires_at` | When the sign-in stops working, in Unix seconds. Use pushes it forward by the sign-in lifetime setting, at most once a minute. | `BIGINT` |
| `last_seen_at` | When the sign-in was last used, in Unix seconds, updated at most once a minute. 0 means not used since it was made. | `BIGINT` |
| `client_label` | A rough description of the browser, such as "Firefox on macOS", shown in the person's list of sign-ins. Empty when the browser didn't say. | `TEXT` |

### device_pairings

One row per pairing code shown on a TV or other device that is asking to be signed in. A signed-in person types the code to approve it; the device then swaps it for a device token and the row is deleted. Codes expire after 10 minutes.

**Kept:** Deleted when redeemed; a code that expires first is deleted by the nightly housekeeping task.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device_code` | SHA-256 hash of the secret the device uses while it waits for approval. The device keeps the secret; the hash can't be used in its place. | `TEXT` · key |
| `user_code` | The short code shown on the device's screen for a person to type, such as BCDF-GHJK. | `TEXT` |
| `user_id` | The person who approved the pairing, from users. NULL while still waiting. | `TEXT` · may be empty · → `users.id` |
| `device_name` | The name the device gave itself, shown when approving it. Empty if it gave none. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the code was shown, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `expires_at` | When the code stops working, in Unix seconds (10 minutes after it was made). | `BIGINT` |
| `approved_at` | When a person approved the code, in Unix seconds. 0 means still waiting. | `BIGINT` |

### device_tokens

One row per paired device, such as a TV app. The device acts as the person who approved it, with that person's current role. A row lasts until the person removes the device or the account is disabled; it has no expiry.

**Kept:** Kept until the person removes the device or the account is disabled.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token_hash` | SHA-256 hash of the device's token. Only the device holds the token; the hash can't be turned back into a working sign-in. | `TEXT` · key |
| `user_id` | The person who approved the device, from users. | `TEXT` · → `users.id` |
| `device_name` | The device's name, shown in the person's list of devices. Empty if it gave none. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the device was paired, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `last_seen_at` | When the device last used Loomarr, in Unix seconds, updated at most once a minute. | `BIGINT` |

### invitations

One row per invitation an admin sends to let a new person in. It reserves a username or a media-server account for 7 days. Finished invitations (redeemed, expired or revoked) are deleted 30 days after they finished.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task deletes redeemed, expired or revoked invitations 30 days after they finished.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the invitation. invitation_grants and contact_addresses point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `kind` | local invites someone to make a Loomarr-only account with the reserved username; library invites the owner of an existing media-server account. | `TEXT` |
| `username` | The username reserved for a local invitation. Empty for a library invitation. | `TEXT` |
| `library_user_id` | The media-server account invited by a library invitation. Empty for a local invitation. | `TEXT` |
| `display_name` | The media-server account's name at the time of inviting. Empty for a local invitation. | `TEXT` |
| `identity_key` | What the invitation reserves, used to stop two pending invitations for the same person. The lowercased, trimmed username for local, or the media-server user id for library. | `TEXT` |
| `role` | The role the new account gets, member or admin. | `TEXT` |
| `status` | pending while it can still be used; redeemed once the person made their account; expired when 7 days passed unused; revoked when an admin cancelled it. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the admin made the invitation, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `expires_at` | When it stops working, in Unix seconds (always 7 days after created_at). | `BIGINT` |
| `terminal_at` | When it was redeemed, revoked or expired, in Unix seconds. 0 while still pending. | `BIGINT` |
| `redeemed_by` | The id of the account created from it, in users. Empty unless redeemed. | `TEXT` |

### invitation_grants

One row per invitation link or QR code handed out for an invitation. When an admin makes a new link, the earlier ones are cancelled; an emailed link is added alongside them. Deleted with their invitation.

**Kept:** Goes with its invitation (deleted when that is).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token_hash` | SHA-256 hash (64 hex characters) of the secret in the link. The link itself is never stored; the hash can't be turned back into a working link. | `TEXT` · key |
| `invitation_id` | The invitation this link opens, from invitations. | `TEXT` · → `invitations.id` |
| `grant_kind` | What the link does. Always activation (making the account). | `TEXT` |
| `conveyance` | How the link reached the person. email means Loomarr sent it to the invited address; copy means an admin copied the link; qr means an admin showed it as a QR code. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the link was made, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `expires_at` | When the link stops working, in Unix seconds. Never later than its invitation's expiry. | `BIGINT` |
| `consumed_at` | When the link was used to make the account, in Unix seconds. 0 means not used. | `BIGINT` |
| `revoked_at` | When the link was cancelled, in Unix seconds, because a newer link replaced it, the invitation was revoked, or another link was used first. 0 means not cancelled. | `BIGINT` |

### password_recoveries

One row per "forgot password" request for a local account. Each lasts 30 minutes, and a new request cancels the person's earlier pending one. Finished requests are deleted 30 days after they finished.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task deletes used, cancelled or expired requests 30 days after they finished.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the request. password_recovery_grants point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `user_id` | The local account being recovered, from users. | `TEXT` · → `users.id` |
| `status` | pending while the link can still be used; redeemed once a new password was set; expired when 30 minutes passed unused; revoked when a newer request replaced it. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the request was made, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `expires_at` | When it stops working, in Unix seconds (always 30 minutes after created_at). | `BIGINT` |
| `terminal_at` | When it was redeemed, revoked or expired, in Unix seconds. 0 while still pending. | `BIGINT` |

### password_recovery_grants

One row per password-reset link emailed for a recovery request. Using one sets the new password, signs the person out everywhere and cancels the request's other links. Deleted with their request.

**Kept:** Goes with its password reset request (deleted when that is).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token_hash` | SHA-256 hash (64 hex characters) of the secret in the reset link. The link itself is never stored; the hash can't be turned back into a working link. | `TEXT` · key |
| `recovery_id` | The request this link belongs to, from password_recoveries. | `TEXT` · → `password_recoveries.id` |
| `created_at` | When the link was made, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `expires_at` | When the link stops working, in Unix seconds. At most 30 minutes after it was made. | `BIGINT` |
| `consumed_at` | When the link was used to set a new password, in Unix seconds. 0 means not used. | `BIGINT` |
| `revoked_at` | When the link was cancelled, in Unix seconds. 0 means not cancelled. | `BIGINT` |

### contact_addresses

Email addresses for people and pending invitations. A person has at most one verified address (the one password recovery goes to) and one pending replacement. An invitation's address moves to the new account when it is redeemed.

**Kept:** Kept while its person or invitation exists (at most two per person); an invitation's address is deleted with the invitation.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `owner_kind` | Whose address it is. user for a person in users; invitation for a pending invitation. | `TEXT` · key |
| `owner_id` | The person's id in users, or the invitation's id in invitations. | `TEXT` · key |
| `email` | The address as entered, for display and sending. | `TEXT` |
| `normalized` | The lowercased address. No two rows may share it, so one address belongs to one owner. | `TEXT` |
| `status` | pending until the owner has shown they receive mail there; verified once they have. Only a verified address is used for password recovery. | `TEXT` · key |
| `provenance` | How Loomarr learned the address. admin means an admin entered it; invitation and self are allowed values that current code does not write. It never implies the address was verified. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the address was added, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `verified_at` | When the address was verified, in Unix seconds. NULL while pending. | `BIGINT` · may be empty |

### user_favourite_channels

One row per channel a person starred as a favourite, used for the guide's Favourites filter. Deleted when the person un-stars it or the channel or person is deleted.

**Kept:** Kept until un-starred; goes with its channel or person (deleted when that is).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_id` | The person, from users. | `TEXT` · key · → `users.id` |
| `channel_id` | The starred channel, from channels. | `TEXT` · key · → `channels.id` |
| `added_at_ms` | When the person starred it, in Unix milliseconds. | `BIGINT` |

### user_recent_channels

One row per channel a person recently tuned to, for the guide's Recent filter. Only each person's 20 most recent channels are kept.

**Kept:** Each person's 20 most recent channels are kept; rows go with their channel or person.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_id` | The person, from users. | `TEXT` · key · → `users.id` |
| `channel_id` | The channel tuned to, from channels. | `TEXT` · key · → `channels.id` |
| `tuned_at_ms` | When the person last tuned to it, in Unix milliseconds. | `BIGINT` |

### user_hidden_ideas

One row per channel idea a person hid on Home. Deleted when they undo the hide or the person is deleted.

**Kept:** Kept until the person undoes the hide; goes with the person.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_id` | The person, from users. | `TEXT` · key · → `users.id` |
| `idea_id` | The hidden idea's stable name, such as genre:comedy. It isn't a link to another table, so the hide survives the library changing. | `TEXT` · key |
| `hidden_at_ms` | When the person hid it, in Unix milliseconds. | `BIGINT` |

### viewings

The watch history: one row per person watching one programme on one channel on one device in the Loomarr apps, from when their player started to when it stopped. Only admins can read it, and the person isn't told. Watching through the media server's Live TV isn't recorded.

**Kept:** Kept until an admin clears it, for one person or everyone; goes with the person.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the row. | `TEXT` · key |
| `user_id` | The person watching, from users. | `TEXT` · → `users.id` |
| `device` | What the household calls the device, such as a paired TV's name or the browser and system. | `TEXT` |
| `channel_id` | The channel watched. It isn't a link to channels, so the history survives the channel being deleted. | `TEXT` |
| `channel_name` | The channel's name when the viewing began. | `TEXT` |
| `programme` | The programme watched; a new row starts when the next programme does. Empty when the guide had nothing for it. | `TEXT` |
| `started_at` | When the player started, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `ended_at` | When the player was last seen, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |

## Channels and the guide

The channels Loomarr runs, what they have aired, and the holidays that decide what is in season for seasonal channels and seasonal filler. The requests that create and refine channels are under Suggestions.

### channels

One row per channel. A channel is created by approving a channel request or by hand. Detaching a channel keeps its row with status `detached`; deleting it removes the row, its airing history and its channel feedback.

**Kept:** Kept until an admin deletes the channel; a detached channel keeps its row.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the channel. Other tables point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `name` | The channel's display name. | `TEXT` |
| `number` | The channel number, which is its position in the guide. Unique. | `INTEGER` |
| `grp` | The group the channel is listed under in the guide. Empty for none. | `TEXT` |
| `logo` | The channel icon's URL, either one of this Loomarr's own image URLs or an outside link. Empty for no icon. | `TEXT` |
| `strategy` | How programmes are ordered onto the timeline. `sequential` plays them in lineup order, `shuffle` rotates them in a shuffled order, and `time_slot` pins them to blocks of the day. | `TEXT` |
| `tunarr_id` | The id of the channel's copy in Tunarr, an outside playout server, kept from the first time Loomarr pushed the channel there. Empty for a channel that never went to Tunarr. | `TEXT` |
| `status` | The channel's state. `building` (being set up), `live` (ready to play), `drifted` (a scheduled programme left the library and was replaced), `empty` (every lineup entry was filtered out, so nothing can air), `paused` (taken off air by an admin but kept), or `detached` (no longer managed by Loomarr). | `TEXT` |
| `shuffle_seed` | The number a shuffled channel's order is drawn from, so it repeats the same way. 0 means it is worked out from the channel id. | `BIGINT` |
| `desired_json` | The last computed schedule, a list of slots. Each slot is a programme, a pending title not yet in the library, a filler break, or flexible padding, with its title, length and episode numbers. | `TEXT` |
| `reconcile_deadline` | When the channel is next due to be checked and brought up to date, in Unix seconds. Moved forward while one check holds it. 0 means due now. | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_at` | When the row last changed, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `policy_json` | The channel's programming rules. What may air (era, genres), who it is for (the audience rating ceiling), how often things may repeat, the ordering, seasonal behaviour and time-of-day rules, plus the rules an admin pinned and the loosening the last check had to apply. `{}` means all defaults. | `TEXT` |
| `broadcast_codec` | The video codec the channel streams in, `h264` or `hevc`, chosen from what most of its titles are encoded in. Every programme and filler clip is converted to it. | `TEXT` |
| `revision` | Counts changes to the row, starting at 1. A change is only saved if it was made from the latest revision, so two edits can't overwrite each other. | `BIGINT` |
| `playout_anchor` | When the channel's current broadcast cycle started, in Unix seconds. The schedule is laid out from this moment. 0 for a channel that has not gone on air yet. | `BIGINT` |
| `created_at` | When the channel was created, in Unix seconds. Never changes. 0 when unknown (a hand-made channel older than the column). | `BIGINT` |
| `intent_json` | The approved channel request the channel was made from (description, era, tone, titles to include or leave out, the chosen name), without one-off refinements. A refine or a scheduled re-curation starts from it. Empty for a hand-made channel. | `TEXT` · may be empty |
| `requested_by` | The person who asked for the channel (users.id). Set when the channel is created and never changed. Null when no member asked, or once that person is deleted. | `TEXT` · may be empty · → `users.id` |
| `from_request` | Whether the channel was made from a member's request rather than by hand. Refine and auto-curate re-run that request; it outlives the job intent_ref names. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `intent_ref` | The channel request job (proposal_jobs.id) the channel was created from, while that job is kept; null once the job is purged, and for a channel made by hand. No two channels share one. | `TEXT` · may be empty · → `proposal_jobs.id` |

### channel_lineup

A channel's approved lineup, one row per title in order: what should play on it. Whether each title becomes a programme or waits as "coming soon" is decided when the channel is checked.

**Kept:** Rewritten whenever the channel is saved; goes with its channel.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel_id` | The channel (a channels id). | `TEXT` · key · → `channels.id` |
| `position` | Where the title sits in the lineup, from 0. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `title_key` | The title (a titles key, such as `movie:tmdb:603`). A title added by hand that nothing has asked for yet has a pending titles row. | `TEXT` · → `titles.key` |
| `entry` | The rest of the entry: its display name, known runtime, any season range or episode selection, the rating, genres and year the channel rules filter on, and its media-server box sets. | `TEXT` |

### airings

What a channel actually broadcast: one row each time an episode or film started playing on a channel. Written when the programme is really streamed, not when it is scheduled. The schedule uses it to prefer what hasn't aired recently. Rows older than 8 days are pruned down to the latest airing of each episode or film; rows go when their channel is deleted.

**Kept:** Airings older than 8 days are pruned to the latest one per episode or film on each channel; goes with its channel (deleted when that is).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel_id` | The channel it aired on (channels.id). | `TEXT` · key · → `channels.id` |
| `library_item_id` | The library item id of the episode or film that aired. | `TEXT` · key |
| `aired_at` | When the programme started, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` · key |
| `recorded_at` | When Loomarr first recorded the airing, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `key` | The key of the lineup title it belongs to, such as `series:tvdb:81189` for an episode of a show. Kept for diagnosis. | `TEXT` |

### scheduled_airings

What a channel's schedule put on air: one row each time an episode or film started on a channel's timeline, whether or not anyone watched. Kept apart from `airings`, which records only what was actually streamed. The schedule reads both, so a channel nobody watches still rotates evenly instead of re-airing something it showed hours ago. Pruned and deleted like `airings`.

**Kept:** Rows older than 8 days are pruned to the latest one per episode or film on each channel; goes with its channel (deleted when that is).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel_id` | The channel it aired on (channels.id). | `TEXT` · key · → `channels.id` |
| `library_item_id` | The library item id of the episode or film. | `TEXT` · key |
| `aired_at` | When the programme started, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` · key |
| `recorded_at` | When Loomarr first recorded the airing, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `key` | The key of the lineup title it belongs to, such as `series:tvdb:81189` for an episode of a show. Kept for diagnosis. | `TEXT` |

### holidays

One row per holiday: when each country keeps it and the words that show a title or clip is about it. Seasonal channel rules and seasonal filler tags read them. Each holiday owns the seasonal tag with the same slug. Rows are added at startup from Loomarr's shipped list and when a seasonal tag is made. An undated holiday is removed when its tag stops being seasonal.

**Kept:** Kept while its seasonal tag exists; an undated holiday is deleted when its tag stops being seasonal.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | The holiday's slug, which is also the slug of its seasonal tag (taxa.slug). | `TEXT` · key · → `taxa.slug` |
| `label` | The holiday's display name. | `TEXT` |
| `position` | The display order. It also settles ties when two holidays are in season at once. | `INTEGER` |
| `words` | JSON with the phrases that tie a title to the holiday. Words that name it in a channel request, its names, look-alike phrases that are not about it (such as "santa monica"), mood words, and genre sets that back up a mood word. | `TEXT` |
| `kept` | JSON list of when countries keep the holiday. Each entry lists countries, the day rule (fixed date, nth or last weekday, or relative to Easter) and the season window around it. `[]` means undated, so its clips air all year. | `TEXT` |
| `air_window` | JSON rule for the time of year when a TV episode first airing then was made for the holiday. Empty when there is none. | `TEXT` · may be empty |
| `members` | JSON list of holiday ids for a group holiday (such as "happy holidays"), which is in season whenever any member is. `[]` for an ordinary holiday. | `TEXT` |
| `name_needs_corroboration` | 1 when the holiday's name alone is not enough to tie a title to it, because the name is also an ordinary title word. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `updated_at` | When the row last changed, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

### holiday_seed_revisions

One row per revision of Loomarr's shipped holiday list that startup has applied. Each revision applies once, so a later change or removal by an admin is never undone. Kept forever.

**Kept:** Kept forever: one small row per shipped list revision, so no revision is applied twice.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | The revision number of the shipped holiday list. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `applied_at` | When it was applied, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

## Suggestions

How Loomarr suggests channels and titles: the requests people make, each run of the suggester, the suggestions waiting for an admin, the Keep and Never choices that steer future picks, and the counts and timings that measure how well the suggestion pipeline works.

### proposal_jobs

One row per run of the channel suggester: a person's channel request, a refine of an existing channel, or a scheduled re-curation. The job's result is a proposal. Finished (`done` or `failed`) jobs are deleted after the `jobs.retention` setting (30 days by default), unless their proposal is still waiting for a decision.

**Kept:** Finished jobs are deleted after `jobs.retention` (30 days by default), unless their proposal still awaits a decision.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the job. Proposals and channels point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `kind` | `suggest` for a request a person made (including a refine), or `recurate` for a scheduled refresh of a channel that allows automatic curation. | `TEXT` |
| `status` | `queued` (waiting for a worker), `running`, `done` (produced a proposal), or `failed`. | `TEXT` |
| `intent_json` | The request: its description and options such as era, tone, titles to include or leave out, and for a refine the change asked for and the channel's current lineup. | `TEXT` |
| `intent_hash` | A fingerprint of the normalised request. A new identical request can reuse a recent `done` job's result instead of running again. | `TEXT` |
| `created_by` | The person who submitted the request (users.id). Empty when no person did. | `TEXT` |
| `last_error` | The detailed error from the last failure, for the logs. Not shown to the requester. | `TEXT` |
| `deadline` | When a queued job is due to run, or when a running job's hold expires and another worker may take it over, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `attempts` | How many times a worker has started the job. | `INTEGER` |
| `created_at` | When the job was submitted, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_at` | When the job last changed, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `failure_code` | Why the job failed, when it did. `no_grounded_titles` (nothing matched titles that exist), `generation_failed` (the AI step failed), `selection_empty` (no titles were chosen), or `budget_exhausted` (it ran out of its allowed work). Empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |
| `workflow_version` | Which version of the job process ran it. 0 is a job from before per-attempt history was kept; 1 is the current process, which records each attempt in proposal_job_attempts. | `INTEGER` |
| `reached_live` | 1 once a channel made from this job has gone live. It stays 1 even if the channel is later paused. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `failure_trace_json` | The bounded record of the candidate titles a failed run considered and why each was kept or dropped, used to explain the failure. Empty when there is none. | `TEXT` · may be empty |
| `channel_id` | The existing channel a refine or re-curation job changes (channels.id); the job goes with that channel. Null for a job that creates a new channel. | `TEXT` · may be empty · → `channels.id` |

### proposal_job_attempts

One row each time a worker started a channel suggester job, so a request's history shows every try. Deleted with its job.

**Kept:** Goes with its job (deleted when that is).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | The job this attempt ran (proposal_jobs.id). | `TEXT` · key · → `proposal_jobs.id` |
| `attempt` | The attempt's number within its job, counting from 1. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `workflow_version` | Which version of the job process ran the attempt. | `INTEGER` |
| `status` | `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `interrupted` (the worker's hold expired while it was still running and the job was taken over). | `TEXT` |
| `started_at` | When the attempt started, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `completed_at` | When the attempt ended, in Unix seconds. 0 while it is running. | `BIGINT` |
| `failure_code` | Why the attempt failed, using the same codes as proposal_jobs.failure_code. Empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |

### proposals

A suggested channel lineup produced by a channel suggester job, waiting for an admin to approve or deny it (shown in the app as a request). Approving it creates or changes a channel.

**Kept:** Denied and superseded proposals are deleted after `proposals.retention` (90 days by default). Approved ones are kept on purpose, one per approval, as the record of who approved each channel; submitted ones wait for an answer.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the proposal. | `TEXT` · key |
| `job_id` | The job that produced it (proposal_jobs.id). | `TEXT` |
| `status` | `submitted` (waiting for a decision), `approved`, `denied`, or `superseded` (replaced by a newer proposal from the same job before anyone decided). | `TEXT` |
| `created_by` | The person who asked for it (users.id). | `TEXT` |
| `decided_by` | The admin who approved or denied it (users.id). Empty until decided. | `TEXT` |
| `deny_reason` | The reason given for a denial. Empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |
| `proposal_json` | The suggestion itself. The request, the proposed channel name, the lineup of titles already in the library, titles to acquire, ranked backups, scores, the rationale and the channel rules. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the proposal was made, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_at` | When the row last changed, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `mod_summary` | What the admin changed before approving, written by Loomarr, such as "dropped 2, added 1". Empty when approved unchanged. | `TEXT` |
| `note` | The admin's message to the requester about the decision. Empty for none. | `TEXT` |
| `approved_at` | When the proposal was approved, in Unix seconds. 0 if it never was. | `BIGINT` |

### discovery_feedback

The Keep, Less like this, Never and Surprise me choices people make about titles, for the whole household or for one channel. Each choice is a new row; the newest per title wins, and a channel's choice overrides the household's. The channel suggester and re-curation read them. A channel's rows are deleted with the channel.

**Kept:** One row per title and scope: the nightly housekeeping task deletes a choice once a newer one replaces it, and a clear once nothing is left under it. A channel's rows go with the channel.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the choice. | `TEXT` · key |
| `actor_id` | The person who made it (users.id), or `api-token` for a choice sent with the API token. | `TEXT` |
| `scope` | Where it applies. `household` for every channel, or `channel` for one channel. | `TEXT` |
| `scope_id` | The channel it applies to (channels.id) when the scope is `channel`, and goes with that channel; null for `household`. | `TEXT` · may be empty · → `channels.id` |
| `target_key` | The title it is about, by its key, such as `movie:tmdb:603`. | `TEXT` |
| `action` | `keep` (favour this title), `less` (less like this, which also lowers titles of its genres), `never` (leave it out), `surprise` (Surprise me, favouring picks unlike it), or `clear` (remove an earlier choice). | `TEXT` |
| `reason` | An optional reason the person gave. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at_ns` | When the choice was made, in Unix nanoseconds. | `BIGINT` |

### quality_receipts

One measured step of the pipeline that suggests and adds titles (retrieval, generation, grounding, approval, acquisition, scheduling) and how it went. Holds counts and timings only, no titles or people. Receipts older than 30 days are rolled into quality_daily_aggregates and deleted.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task rolls receipts older than 30 days into daily totals and deletes them.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `idempotency_key` | An opaque hash identifying the step, so the same step is never counted twice. | `TEXT` · key |
| `occurred_at` | When the step happened, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `stage` | The pipeline step. `retrieval`, `generation`, `grounding`, `approval`, `acquisition` or `scheduling`. | `TEXT` |
| `outcome` | How it went, from a set fixed per stage. retrieval is succeeded, empty or failed; generation is succeeded, abstained or failed; grounding is accepted or rejected; approval is approved or declined; acquisition is playable or failed; scheduling is scheduled or failed. | `TEXT` |
| `duration_ms` | How long the step took, in milliseconds. 0 when not measured. | `BIGINT` |
| `tool_calls` | How many tool calls the model made during the step. | `INTEGER` |
| `candidate_count` | How many candidate titles the step surfaced. | `INTEGER` |
| `cost_nanos` | What the step cost, in billionths of a US dollar. | `BIGINT` |
| `run_snapshot_id` | The evaluation run it belongs to (quality_run_snapshots.id). Empty for ordinary use of the app. | `TEXT` · may be empty · → `quality_run_snapshots.id` |

### quality_daily_aggregates

Daily totals of suggestion-quality receipts, one row per day, stage, outcome and evaluation run. Kept for two years. This is what the admin discovery-quality export downloads.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task deletes days older than two years.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `day` | The UTC day, as YYYY-MM-DD. | `TEXT` · key |
| `stage` | The pipeline step, with the same values as quality_receipts.stage. | `TEXT` · key |
| `outcome` | How the steps went, with the same values as quality_receipts.outcome. | `TEXT` · key |
| `run_snapshot_id` | The evaluation run (quality_run_snapshots.id), or empty for ordinary use. | `TEXT` · key |
| `observation_count` | How many receipts were rolled into the row. | `BIGINT` |
| `duration_ms` | Total time of those steps, in milliseconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `tool_calls` | Total tool calls. | `BIGINT` |
| `candidate_count` | Total candidate titles surfaced. | `BIGINT` |
| `cost_nanos` | Total cost, in billionths of a US dollar. | `BIGINT` |

### quality_run_snapshots

The fixed facts about one suggestion-quality evaluation run (the model, provider and test set it used), so receipts and daily totals can be compared across runs. No part of the running app writes rows today. Snapshots no longer referenced are trimmed to the newest 256.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task keeps the newest 256 snapshots that nothing refers to any more.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the snapshot, derived from its facts (eval-<hash>). Receipts and daily totals point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `schema_version` | Version of the snapshot format. | `INTEGER` |
| `corpus_version` | Version of the test set the run was scored on. | `TEXT` |
| `requested_model` | The model the run asked for. | `TEXT` |
| `resolved_model` | The model that actually answered, when every call reported the same one. Empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |
| `provider` | The AI provider. `unknown`, `ollama`, `openrouter` or `custom`. | `TEXT` |
| `budget_profile` | The spending profile the run used. | `TEXT` |
| `application_version` | The Loomarr version (and commit) that ran it. | `TEXT` |
| `accounting_available` | 1 when the provider reported costs for the run. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `created_at` | When the run was made, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |

## Your library

Loomarr scans the household's media folders itself, matches each movie and show it finds to a TMDB title, and asks a person when it can't tell (Needs you). These tables hold the folders, the files found in them, the titles they make up and their details, the household's collections, the movies and shows requested through Seerr or the arr apps, and the artwork shown for all of them.

### library_roots

One row per local folder Loomarr may walk for media. A folder is added when a media server or arr reports it or when someone types it in. A folder that is not in use, not typed by hand and named by no path mapping is dropped.

**Kept:** Kept while the folder is in use, typed by hand or named by a path mapping; dropped otherwise, when discovery runs or someone stops using a hand-typed folder.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | The folder as Loomarr opens it, an absolute path. | `TEXT` · key |
| `in_use` | 1 when the folder is confirmed for scanning. A discovered folder starts at 0; one typed by hand starts at 1. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `readable` | 1 when the last check could open the folder. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `checked_at_ms` | When the folder was last checked for readability, in Unix milliseconds; 0 means never. | `INTEGER` |
| `by_hand` | 1 when someone typed the folder in rather than a media server or arr reporting it. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `added_at_ms` | When the folder was added, in Unix milliseconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `scanned_at_ms` | When a walk of the folder last completed, in Unix milliseconds; 0 means never. | `INTEGER` |
| `empty` | 1 when the last check opened the folder and found nothing in it, which usually means the share behind a mount point isn't mounted. Always 0 when the folder isn't readable. | `BOOLEAN` |

### library_root_paths

The path map. One row per folder a media server or arr reports, saying which local folder it is. Discovery rewrites rows unless someone set them by hand; a row the app stops reporting is dropped once that app answers without it.

**Kept:** Kept while the app keeps reporting the folder or someone set it by hand; dropped when a full discovery from that app no longer lists it.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authority` | The app that reported the folder, one of emby, jellyfin, sonarr or radarr. | `TEXT` · key |
| `authority_path` | The folder as that app names it. | `TEXT` · key |
| `root_path` | The local folder it maps to (a library_roots path), or empty when no local folder was found for it. | `TEXT` |
| `by_hand` | 1 when someone set the mapping by hand. Discovery never rewrites such a row. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `seen_at_ms` | When the app last reported the folder, or the mapping was last set, in Unix milliseconds. | `INTEGER` |

### library_files

One row per media file the scanner found under an in-use folder. A file the scanner no longer finds keeps its row with a missing time; all of a folder's rows go when the folder is forgotten.

**Kept:** Kept while its folder is in use. A file a walk stopped finding is deleted by the nightly housekeeping 180 days later, unless its removal is still waiting for a person; every row of a folder is deleted when the folder stops being in use.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | The file as Loomarr opens it, an absolute path. | `TEXT` · key |
| `root` | The folder it was found under (a library_roots path). | `TEXT` |
| `size_bytes` | The file's size in bytes at the last walk. | `INTEGER` |
| `modified_ns` | The file's modification time at the last walk, in Unix nanoseconds. With the size it marks the file's revision, so an unchanged file is never opened again. | `INTEGER` |
| `identity` | A digest of what said what the file is (its arr record, ids in its name, its NFO sidecar) when it was last written to the library. Cleared to make the scanner write the file again. | `TEXT` |
| `kind` | What the file was last written as, one of movie, episode or extra; empty for a problem file. | `TEXT` |
| `header` | Whether the file's container header has been read. One of pending (not yet), read, or failed (it can't be read, so the file can't be played). | `TEXT` |
| `problem` | Why the file is skipped, or empty for none. One of disc_image (a disc image), identity_conflict (what names the file disagrees), or invalid_facts (the library refused what was read from it). | `TEXT` |
| `held` | 1 when a walk no longer found the file and that walk's removals are waiting for a person to confirm them. A held file still counts as present. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `seen_at_ms` | When a walk last found the file, in Unix milliseconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `missing_at_ms` | When a walk stopped finding the file, in Unix milliseconds; 0 means it is present. | `INTEGER` |
| `inventory_item_id` | The title the file was last written as (a library_items id); null until known. | `TEXT` · may be empty · → `library_items.id` |
| `inventory_series_id` | For an episode, its show (a library_items id); null otherwise or until known. | `TEXT` · may be empty · → `library_items.id` |

### library_items

One row per movie, show and episode the scanner wrote, with the details shown on the Library pages. Rewritten each time the title is written; a title whose files have gone keeps its row, so it finds its collections and answer again if it comes back. Whether it is present comes from library_files.

**Kept:** A title that leaves the library keeps its row, so it finds its details and collections again if it comes back. The nightly housekeeping deletes a row a year after it last changed once nothing is left of it: no importer report, no file, no episode, no collection, and no title, airing, channel or open request naming it. Its candidates and images go with it; a person's answer for it is kept.

**The title.** What every list and search shows for a title.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the title. library_files, collections and the rows below point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `kind` | One of movie, series or episode. | `TEXT` |
| `name` | The title's name. | `TEXT` |
| `sort_name` | The lower-case name it sorts by. | `TEXT` |
| `year` | The year, or 0 when unknown. | `INTEGER` |
| `updated_at_ms` | When the row was last written, in Unix milliseconds. | `INTEGER` |

**Where it was found.** One scan origin per title, which a person's answer is kept against.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `origin_authority` | The scanned folder the title was found in, as scan: followed by a digest of the folder's path. With origin_key it is the title's scan origin, which a person's answer is kept against. | `TEXT` |
| `origin_key` | Where in that folder the title was found, a digest of a movie's file (file:...) or a show's folder (series:dir:...). | `TEXT` |

**Which title it is.** The one match the library settled on and how. Candidates and answers that compete for it live in library_candidates and library_answers.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` | The library_catalog row its details come from, written provider:kind:id (for example tmdb:movie:603); empty for none. | `TEXT` |
| `grounded` | 1 when something gives the title an id (match_basis is not empty). A movie or show at 0 with no answer is listed in Needs you. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `searched` | The name, year and evidence the title was last searched for on TMDB to find candidates; empty when never searched. A title is searched again only when this would change. | `TEXT` |
| `match_basis` | What said which title it is. One of manager (an arr tracks it), embedded_id (an id in the file or folder name), sidecar (an NFO file), link (a person's answer), or search (one TMDB result agreed); empty for nothing. Set for movies and shows only. | `TEXT` |
| `match_app` | The app that said it, one of sonarr, radarr, nfo or tmdb; empty for evidence Loomarr finds itself. | `TEXT` |
| `match_page` | The title's page in that app, for a person to open; empty when it has none. | `TEXT` |
| `needs_noticed` | 1 once a daily Needs you notice has counted the title as new, so a restart neither repeats nor loses a notice. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `set_key` | For a movie, the library_catalog row of the TMDB collection it belongs to (for example tmdb_collection:collection:10); empty for none. Lets the Collections page say "you have 3 of 4". | `TEXT` |

**Details.** The single value shown for each detail. Lists (genres, people, artwork) live in their own tables.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `original_title` | The title in its original language, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `overview` | The description, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `premiere_date` | The release or first-air date as the source gave it, such as 2013-05-01; empty when unknown. | `TEXT` |
| `rating` | The content rating, such as TV-PG; empty when unknown. An episode with no rating of its own takes its show's. | `TEXT` |
| `score` | The community score from 0 to 10; 0 when unknown. | `REAL` |
| `runtime_ms` | The running time in milliseconds; 0 when unknown. | `INTEGER` |
| `tagline` | The one-line pitch printed on a poster; empty when unknown. | `TEXT` |
| `trailer` | The web page that plays the title's trailer; empty when it has none. | `TEXT` |

**An episode's place.** An episode belongs to one show at one season and number; movies and shows leave these empty.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `season` | An episode's season number; 0 for movies and shows. | `INTEGER` |
| `episode` | An episode's episode number; 0 for movies and shows. | `INTEGER` |
| `episode_end` | The last episode number a multi-episode file covers; 0 for a single episode. | `INTEGER` |
| `series_authority` | An episode's show, by the scan folder part of the show's scan origin; empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |
| `series_key` | An episode's show, by the folder part of the show's scan origin; empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |
| `series_id` | An episode's show (a library_items id), filled once both the episode and the show are written; null otherwise. | `TEXT` · may be empty · → `library_items.id` |
| `unnumbered` | 1 for an episode its show's catalog could not number, because the catalog numbers the show in more than one order or its seasons end elsewhere than the disk's, and nobody has said which order the show's files follow. It keeps its file's name and number, and its show is in Needs you. 0 otherwise. | `BOOLEAN` |

**Which app supplied each detail.** One source per detail above, so the detail page can say where each one came from.

| Column | What it holds | Type |

| `overview_from` | The app that supplied the description; empty when unknown. | `TEXT` |
| `premiere_from` | The app that supplied the premiere date; empty when unknown. | `TEXT` |
| `rating_from` | The app that supplied the rating, or show when an episode's rating is its show's; empty when unknown. | `TEXT` |
| `score_from` | The app that supplied the score; empty when unknown. | `TEXT` |
| `runtime_from` | The app that supplied the running time; empty when unknown. | `TEXT` |

Everyone credited on a title in the library. A person with a TMDB id is one row wherever they are credited; one a source names without it is kept by name, unlinked. A person's name and photo are the latest any title gave. A row outlives the titles that credited it.

### library_catalog

What TMDB says about a title or a TMDB collection, cached so a scan never has to ask it. A row is added when a title names it, and refreshed in the background.

**Kept:** Kept while a library title names it. One no title names is deleted by the nightly housekeeping a year after it was fetched, or after a year of failed fetches; one asked for and not yet tried is kept until it is.

| --- | --- | --- |

| `external_id` | The id the catalog knows it by. | `TEXT` · key |
| `record` | The catalog's record as JSON (names, description, ids, artwork and so on). Empty until fetched, and empty after the catalog said it has no such title. | `TEXT` |
| `fetched_at_ms` | When the record was last fetched, in Unix milliseconds; 0 means never. | `INTEGER` |
| `retry_at_ms` | After a failed fetch, the time before which it is not tried again, in Unix milliseconds; 0 for none. | `INTEGER` |
| `version` | The shape of record it was fetched in. A record of an older shape than its kind is read in now is fetched again first, as if it had never been fetched. | `INTEGER` |
| `language` | The language the record was fetched in, such as en-US; empty before languages were noted. A record in another language than the household's is fetched again first. | `TEXT` |
| `changed` | 1 when the catalog's nightly change feed named the record after it was fetched; it is fetched again ahead of the refresh, which sets it back to 0. | `BOOLEAN` |

### titles

One row per movie or show a channel wants that has gone through Seerr or the arr apps, tracking it from wanted to in the library (or given up on). A title added to a lineup by hand that nothing has asked for yet has a pending row, so every lineup entry names a row here.

**Kept:** A title in the library or given up on that no channel's lineup and no open request names is deleted by the nightly housekeeping 180 days after it last changed; picked again, it is requested afresh. A title still on its way is kept. A pending row goes as soon as no lineup names it.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | Identifies the title, as series:tvdb:id for a show with a TVDB id, otherwise movie:tmdb:id or series:tmdb:id. | `TEXT` · key |
| `title_json` | The title as JSON, with its media type (movie or series), TMDB and TVDB ids, name, year and, for a show, the seasons wanted (none listed means all). | `TEXT` |
| `state` | Where it is. One of pending (on a lineup, but nothing has asked for it; read as no record), wanted (not yet accepted by Seerr or an arr), requested (accepted, waiting for a release), downloading (a release was grabbed), available (in the library), or unavailable (given up on). | `TEXT` |
| `library_id` | The media server's id for the title once it is in the library; empty before. | `TEXT` |
| `requested_at` | When Seerr or an arr first accepted the request, in Unix seconds; 0 means not yet. | `BIGINT` |
| `deadline` | When a requested or downloading title is given up on, in Unix seconds; it is also pushed forward briefly while a check is working on the title. 0 for none. | `BIGINT` |
| `attempts` | How many times sending the request has failed. | `INTEGER` |
| `last_error` | The last error sending or tracking the request, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `updated_at` | When the row last changed state, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `progress` | How much of the download is done, from 0 to 1. | `REAL` |
| `eta_text` | The download's time left, as the arr words it; empty when unknown. | `TEXT` |
| `download_status` | The arr's queue status, such as downloading, warning or stalled; empty when none. | `TEXT` |
| `arrived_at` | When the title arrived in the library after being requested, in Unix seconds. 0 when it never arrived or was already in the library when picked. | `BIGINT` |
| `episodes_have` | For a downloading show, how many wanted episodes are on disk; 0 otherwise. | `INTEGER` |
| `episodes_wanted` | For a downloading show, how many episodes are wanted; 0 otherwise. | `INTEGER` |

### images

One row per piece of artwork (posters, channel icons, clip stills and so on). The image bytes are files on disk named by their hash, never in the database. TMDB artwork's files are deleted six months after it was fetched, as TMDB's terms require, and the row waits to be fetched again.

**Kept:** Kept while something uses the image; the daily image clean-up deletes images nothing refers to, and a re-fetched image with new bytes replaces its old row.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hash` | The SHA-256 of the original bytes, in hex. Its identity and file name. Artwork not yet downloaded is keyed by a hash of its URL until the bytes arrive. | `TEXT` · key |
| `origin` | Where the bytes came from, which decides whether they can be got back after a restore. One of upload (a person uploaded it; not recoverable), remote (downloaded from TMDB or a media server; recoverable from source_url), extracted (made from local media, such as a clip still or a poster beside a file; recoverable), or generated (made by Loomarr; treated as not recoverable). | `TEXT` |
| `source_url` | The URL a remote image was downloaded from; empty for every other origin. | `TEXT` |
| `visibility` | Who may fetch it. public needs no sign-in (a channel icon other apps fetch); member needs a signed-in person. | `TEXT` |
| `role` | What the image is for, which sets its sizes and shape. One of poster, backdrop, icon, thumb (a clip still), watermark (a channel's on-screen logo) or logo (a title's clear logo, kept with its transparency, so it has no JPEG size). | `TEXT` |
| `mime` | The original's file type, such as image/png. | `TEXT` |
| `width` | The original's width in pixels. | `INTEGER` |
| `height` | The original's height in pixels. | `INTEGER` |
| `bytes` | The original's size in bytes. | `INTEGER` |
| `animated` | 1 when the original moves (a clip's hover loop). | `BOOLEAN` |
| `placeholder` | A tiny blurred preview (a ThumbHash, base64) shown while the image loads. | `TEXT` |
| `dominant_hex` | The image's average colour, as | `TEXT` |
| `meta` | A JSON object of free-form notes about the image, such as attribution, licence or upstream ids. {} when there are none. | `TEXT` |
| `origin_fetched_at` | When a remote image's bytes were downloaded, in Unix seconds; 0 means not downloaded yet. Drives the six-month expiry for TMDB artwork. | `INTEGER` |
| `created_at` | When the image was first stored, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `updated_at` | When the row last changed, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `last_used_at` | When the image was last used, in Unix seconds. Older images lose their resized copies first when space runs short. | `INTEGER` |
| `frame_count` | How many frames the original has; 1 for a still image. | `INTEGER` |
| `duration_ms` | An animation's length in milliseconds; 0 for a still image. | `INTEGER` |
| `loop_count` | How many times an animation plays. Empty (NULL) for a still image, 0 for an endless loop. | `INTEGER` · may be empty |

### clip_images

A clip's images, such as its thumbnail. One of five tables saying what each image is used for, one per kind of owner, so each owner is a real reference; an image with no row in any of them is cleaned up.

**Kept:** Goes with its clip or its image; a clip re-keyed to new bytes keeps its rows.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_hash` | The clip (a clips hash). | `TEXT` · key · → `clips.hash` |
| `role` | What the image is for, such as thumb. | `TEXT` · key |
| `image_hash` | The image (an images hash). | `TEXT` · key · → `images.hash` |

### filler_split_proposal_images

The stills a proposed split shows, one per cut.

**Kept:** Goes with its proposal or its image.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proposal_id` | The proposal (a filler_split_proposals id). | `TEXT` · key · → `filler_split_proposals.id` |
| `role` | What the image is for, such as thumb. | `TEXT` · key |
| `image_hash` | The image (an images hash). | `TEXT` · key · → `images.hash` |

### channel_images

A channel's icon and watermark.

**Kept:** Goes with its channel or its image; replaced when the icon or watermark changes.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel_id` | The channel (a channels id). | `TEXT` · key · → `channels.id` |
| `role` | What the image is for, icon or watermark. | `TEXT` · key |
| `image_hash` | The image (an images hash). | `TEXT` · key · → `images.hash` |

### library_item_images

A title's poster, backdrop and logo, the one record of which image each is.

**Kept:** Goes with its title or its image; a kind replaces only its own role's row.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item_id` | The title (a library_items id). | `TEXT` · key · → `library_items.id` |
| `role` | What the image is for, one of poster, backdrop or logo. | `TEXT` · key |
| `image_hash` | The image (an images hash). | `TEXT` · key · → `images.hash` |

### library_candidate_images

The posters of what a search found for a title that Needs you.

**Kept:** Goes with its title or its image.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item_id` | The title the candidates are for (a library_items id). | `TEXT` · key · → `library_items.id` |
| `role` | What the image is for, poster. | `TEXT` · key |
| `image_hash` | The image (an images hash). | `TEXT` · key · → `images.hash` |

### image_derivatives

One resized copy of an image in one format, stored as a file on disk. Made on demand or in the background; any row can be deleted to free space and costs only a re-encode. Deleted with the image.

**Kept:** Goes with its image; the least recently used copies are deleted when the image cache is over its size budget, and all of an image's copies when its bytes expire.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image_hash` | The original image (an images hash). | `TEXT` · key · → `images.hash` |
| `recipe` | The encoder settings it was made with, such as loomarr-rendition-v2. Changed settings make new copies rather than reusing old ones. | `TEXT` · key |
| `format` | The file format, one of avif, webp or jpeg. | `TEXT` · key |
| `width` | The copy's width in pixels. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `bytes` | The copy's size in bytes. | `INTEGER` |
| `output_hash` | The SHA-256 of the copy's bytes, in hex; empty for copies made before it was recorded. | `TEXT` |
| `path` | Where the copy's file is on disk. | `TEXT` |
| `animated` | 1 when the copy keeps the original's motion. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `created_at` | When the copy was made, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

## Media inventory

Loomarr's record of every movie, show and episode its importers have reported, and the files that play them. An importer is a library scan of one folder or an Emby or Jellyfin server. When two importers report the same title (they share an id such as a TMDB number), their reports join one item. The measurements Loomarr takes of each file are kept here too.

### inventory_items

One row per movie, show or episode, however many importers report it. Created by the first report. Items are kept when an importer stops seeing them (the report is marked missing instead).

**Kept:** Deleted when its last report moves to another item, or by the nightly housekeeping once its last report was deleted for being missing 180 days.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the item. Other inventory tables point here, and the library's tables name it as their inventory item. | `TEXT` · key |
| `kind` | What the item is, as the importer names it, lowercased. The library scan writes `movie`, `series` or `episode`, matching the media server's names for them. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the item was first reported, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_at` | When a report last updated the item, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |

### inventory_item_origins

One importer's latest report of one item. Replaced each time that importer reports the item again. Kept when the importer no longer sees it, with missing_at set.

**Kept:** Marked missing when the importer stops seeing it, and cleared if it comes back. The nightly housekeeping deletes it 180 days after it went missing, with its source reports.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authority_id` | The importer that reported it. `scan:` and a fingerprint of the scanned folder, or `library:emby:` or `library:jellyfin:` and a fingerprint of the server's address. | `TEXT` · key |
| `external_item_id` | The importer's own id for the item, unique only within that importer. The media server's item id, or for a library scan a fingerprint of the file's path (`file:`) or the show's folder (`series:dir:`). | `TEXT` · key |
| `item_id` | The item the report belongs to (inventory_items.id). | `TEXT` · → `inventory_items.id` |
| `observation_json` | What the importer reported: names, overview, genres, tags, studios, people, year, season and episode numbers, premiere date, rating, score, runtime, artwork and related ids. A coverage map tells a field that is known to be empty apart from one that was not reported. | `TEXT` |
| `observed_at` | When this report was taken, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `last_seen_at` | When the importer last reported the item, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `missing_at` | When the importer stopped seeing the item, in Unix seconds. Empty while it is present. Cleared if the item comes back. | `BIGINT` · may be empty |

### inventory_external_ids

The outside ids one importer's report gives an item, such as its TMDB, TVDB or IMDb number. Matching ids are how reports of the same title from different importers join one item. Replaced with each new report; deleted with the report or the item.

**Kept:** Replaced with each new report; a report marked missing keeps its last ids.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item_id` | The item the id belongs to (inventory_items.id). | `TEXT` · → `inventory_items.id` |
| `authority_id` | The importer whose report gave the id (part of inventory_item_origins). | `TEXT` · key · → `inventory_item_origins.authority_id` |
| `external_item_id` | The importer's id for the item (part of inventory_item_origins). | `TEXT` · key · → `inventory_item_origins.external_item_id` |
| `namespace` | Which id system the id comes from, lowercased, such as `tmdb`, `tvdb` or `imdb`. | `TEXT` · key |
| `external_id` | The id within that system. | `TEXT` · key |

### inventory_sources

One playable file (or media server version) of an item. Created by the first report that lists it; it moves with its report if the report joins another item.

**Kept:** Goes with its item. A source left with no report is deleted by the nightly housekeeping, with its measurement and analysis, once it is 180 days old.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the source. Other inventory tables and playout point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `item_id` | The item the source plays (inventory_items.id). | `TEXT` · → `inventory_items.id` |
| `kind` | `local_file` for a file the library scan found, or `library_original` for a media server's own copy of the item. | `TEXT` |
| `revision` | Identifies the exact bytes of the source. For a scanned file, its size and modified time (`stat:`); for a media server copy, its ETag (`etag:`) or a fingerprint of its details (`observed:`). When it changes, the source's measurement and analysis are thrown away. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the source was first reported, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_at` | When a report last updated the source, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |

### inventory_source_origins

One importer's latest report of one source of an item. Replaced each time that importer reports it again. Kept when the importer no longer sees it, with missing_at set. Deleted with the source or the item's report.

**Kept:** Marked missing when the importer stops seeing it. The nightly housekeeping deletes it 180 days after it went missing; it also goes with its source or its item's report.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authority_id` | The importer that reported it (part of inventory_item_origins). | `TEXT` · key · → `inventory_item_origins.authority_id` |
| `external_item_id` | The importer's id for the item (part of inventory_item_origins). | `TEXT` · key · → `inventory_item_origins.external_item_id` |
| `external_source_id` | The importer's id for this source within the item. The media server's source id, or `file` for a scanned file. | `TEXT` · key |
| `source_id` | The source the report belongs to (inventory_sources.id). | `TEXT` · → `inventory_sources.id` |
| `locator_json` | Where to find the source. A scanned file's path, or the media server item and source ids (never a URL or credentials). | `TEXT` |
| `observation_json` | What the importer reported about the file. Container, size, bitrate, length, modified time and each video, audio and subtitle stream's details, with a coverage map of what was reported. | `TEXT` |
| `observed_at` | When this report was taken, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `last_seen_at` | When the importer last reported the source, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `missing_at` | When the importer stopped seeing the source, in Unix seconds. Empty while it is present. | `BIGINT` · may be empty |

### inventory_source_measurements

The stream details Loomarr measured itself by reading the file, for the source's current revision. Written the first time the source plays or by the measurement job, and used instead of what an importer reported when it is newer. Deleted when the source's revision changes or the source goes.

**Kept:** At most one row per source; thrown away when the source's file changes.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source_id` | The source measured (inventory_sources.id). | `TEXT` · key · → `inventory_sources.id` |
| `source_revision` | The source revision that was measured. | `TEXT` |
| `observation_json` | The measured details. Container, length, bitrate and each stream (codec, language, channels, size, frame rate, colour, HDR), with a coverage map that also says when the file has no audio. | `TEXT` |
| `observed_at` | When it was measured, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |

### inventory_source_analysis

Loomarr's deeper analysis of a source's current revision. The seek points, loudness, natural break points and the picture area. Written by the measurement job and read by playout and the schedule. Replaced on re-analysis; deleted when the revision changes or the source goes.

**Kept:** At most one row per source; replaced on re-analysis, dropped when the file changes.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source_id` | The source analysed (inventory_sources.id). | `TEXT` · key · → `inventory_sources.id` |
| `source_revision` | The source revision that was analysed. | `TEXT` |
| `schema_version` | The version of the analysis format. A row written by any other version is treated as not analysed, and an older one is analysed again. | `INTEGER` |
| `keyframes` | The keyframe index (the points playback can start or cut at), packed as binary: each keyframe's time in milliseconds and byte position. | `BLOB` |
| `keyframe_count` | How many keyframes the index holds. | `INTEGER` |
| `integrated_lufs` | The overall loudness of the audio, in LUFS. Empty when the source has no audio. | `DOUBLE PRECISION` · may be empty |
| `true_peak_dbtp` | The loudest audio peak, in dBTP. Empty when the source has no audio or no peak was found. | `DOUBLE PRECISION` · may be empty |
| `breaks_json` | The places an ad break could go without cutting into a scene. Each has its time, where it came from (`chapter` or `fade`), the nearest keyframe, how long the black and silent stretch lasted, and a confidence from 0 to 1. | `TEXT` |
| `analyzed_at` | When it was analysed, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `active_picture_json` | The part of the frame that is picture, without letterbox or pillarbox bars, as {x, y, w, h} in source pixels. The channel logo is placed by its corner. Empty when unknown (no video, or every sampled frame was black). | `TEXT` · may be empty |

## Filler clips

Filler is the short clips (vintage ads, station promos, bumpers, PSAs) that play in the breaks between shows. These tables remember the clip catalog and its tags, where clips come from and how they were downloaded, how each clip was prepared and checked, what aired, and the directory of TV stations a clip can name.

### clips

One row per filler clip, identified by a hash of its bytes. The folder scan and intake add rows; a row goes away when its file is no longer in any clip folder, unless its recording was deliberately reclaimed (reaped_at), in which case the row stays. A clip's category is not stored: it is the most specific product tag in clip_tags.

**Kept:** Kept while its file is in a clip folder; the folder scan deletes the rest, except reclaimed compilations, which stay. A copy merged into a better copy is deleted too.

**The file.** One file per clip, and every read of a clip needs it; the hash is the clip's identity.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hash` | The clip's identity: a 64-character hex hash sampled from its bytes. Two copies of the same file are one clip. Other filler tables point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `path` | Where the file is, relative to the clip folder (for example a3/f9/<hash>.mp4). A location, not an identity. | `TEXT` |
| `tunarr_program_id` | The Tunarr program id for this clip when Tunarr knows it; NULL on installs without Tunarr. | `TEXT` · may be empty |
| `duration_ms` | Length of the clip in milliseconds, measured from the file. | `INTEGER` |
| `source` | Where the clip came from: the id of the registered filler source that downloaded it (such as archive:<collection>), or filler-dir for a file dropped into the clip folder. | `TEXT` |
| `quality` | Resolution label such as 1080p or 480p, from the measured video height. Empty for an audio-only clip. Shown only; it does not affect selection by default. | `TEXT` |
| `license` | The licence URL the source declared for the clip. Empty means unknown, never public domain. | `TEXT` |
| `updated_at` | When the row last changed, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `created_at` | When the clip was first added to the catalog, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

**What it is.** The facts selection and research read for every clip, one value each. Repeated facts (product tags, defects, research) already live in their own tables.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Display name: a title from the source or its sidecar file, a name built from grounded evidence, one a person wrote, or the filename. | `TEXT` |
| `role` | What the clip is: unclassified (not yet known), commercial, bumper, station_id, psa, trailer, interstitial, political or news. | `TEXT` |
| `era` | The year the clip is from, such as 1994; a year ending in 0 means the decade. 0 means not known. | `INTEGER` |
| `audience` | Who the clip suits: kids, family, general or late_night. Empty when not yet tagged. | `TEXT` |
| `language` | Spoken language detected in the clip, as a language code such as en. Empty means not checked yet; none means checked and there is no speech. | `TEXT` |
| `transcript` | The clip's spoken words, once transcribed. Empty when not transcribed or wordless. | `TEXT` |
| `brand` | The advertiser the clip is for, such as a cereal or car maker. Kept only when the name appears in the clip's text, transcript or on-screen text; empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |
| `visible_text` | Text a vision model read off the clip's frames, such as a logo, product name or year. Brands and eras from vision are kept only when supported by this text. | `TEXT` |
| `enrichment_revision` | A counter that goes up when the clip's name, role, source, transcript or on-screen text changes. Research and tagging results record the revision they were made from, so a change makes them run again. | `INTEGER` |
| `name_source` | Where the name came from: source (a title inside the media), sidecar (the downloaded info file), grounded (built from evidence such as the brand), curated (written by a person), filename (never shown to viewers), or unknown. | `TEXT` |

**Where and when it aired.** One place and date per clip, filtered on together with the clip when channels pick filler for their region.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `geographic_scope` | How widely the clip aired: national, local (one station's own material) or unknown. | `TEXT` |
| `country` | The country the clip aired in, as a two-letter ISO code. Empty when not known. | `TEXT` |
| `network` | The broadcast network the clip is tied to, when known from evidence. | `TEXT` |
| `station` | The broadcast station the clip belongs to, as an id in Loomarr's station directory. A local clip is local to this station. | `TEXT` |
| `air_date` | The date the clip was broadcast, as YYYY-MM-DD, when known from evidence. | `TEXT` |
| `geo_evidence` | The source text that supports the clip's geography, or operator when a person set it. | `TEXT` |

**Whether it can air.** Every read of the pool checks these first, so they stay beside the clip rather than behind a join.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `removed_at` | When the clip was removed from the catalog, in Unix seconds; 0 means present. The file is kept; a removed clip is not listed or aired. | `INTEGER` |
| `held` | 1 while the clip is recorded but not yet playable: every new clip starts held and is released when its preparation finishes and it is ready. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `reaped_at` | When the clip's file was deleted on purpose while its row was kept, in Unix seconds: a composite whose recording was reclaimed after splitting, or a copy retired for failing the defect check. NULL means the file is still there. | `INTEGER` · may be empty |
| `placement` | Where a ready clip may be scheduled: break_body (inside a break), bookend (opening or closing a break) or not_playable. Set when the clip becomes ready. | `TEXT` |

**Composites.** A clip cut from a longer recording names that one recording; a recording names none.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `is_composite` | 1 when the file is a recorded break holding many ads. A composite never airs itself; the clips split out of it do. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `parent_hash` | The composite clip this clip was split out of. Empty for a clip that was not split from one. | `TEXT` |

**Rotation totals.** Running totals rotation reads with the pool. Each airing itself is kept in filler_airings.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `play_count` | How many times Loomarr's own playout has aired the clip. Channels played through Tunarr never report plays, so their clips stay at 0. | `INTEGER` |
| `last_played_at` | When Loomarr's playout last aired the clip, in Unix seconds; 0 means never. | `INTEGER` |

**Pictures.** One still and one hover preview per clip, shown wherever the clip is listed.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `thumbnail` | Still image file, relative to the thumbnail cache folder. Empty when not generated yet. | `TEXT` |
| `preview` | Short animated preview shown on hover, relative to the preview cache folder. Empty when not generated yet. | `TEXT` |
| `thumb_image_hash` | The image service's id for the still image. Empty when not stored there yet. | `TEXT` |
| `hover_image_hash` | The image service's id for the hover preview. Empty when not stored there yet. | `TEXT` |


### clip_tags

Each tag a clip carries from the taxonomy (taxa). Rows are rewritten whenever a clip is tagged or the taxonomy changes.

**Kept:** Rewritten on each retag and removed with a deleted tag or a merged copy. Tags of a clip the folder scan removed are deleted by the nightly housekeeping, unless the catalog is empty (an unmounted drive).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
