| `clip_hash` | The clip that carries the tag (clips.hash). | `TEXT` · key |
| `taxon` | The tag (taxa.slug). | `TEXT` · key |
| `leaf` | 1 when the tag was set directly on the clip by a person or the tagger. 0 when it was added automatically because the clip carries a more specific tag beneath it (beer adds alcohol and drinks). | `BOOLEAN` |

### taxa

The tag vocabulary for clips, one row per tag, arranged as trees on separate axes. Loomarr seeds it on first start and adds new shipped tags over time; operators can edit and delete tags.

**Kept:** Kept until an operator deletes the tag.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slug` | The tag's stable id, such as beer. Tag rows elsewhere point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `label` | The tag's display name. | `TEXT` |
| `parent` | The slug of the broader tag above this one on the same axis. Empty for a top-level tag. | `TEXT` |
| `axis` | Which kind of tag it is: product (what the clip sells), format (what the clip is, such as a PSA or trailer), seasonal (when it belongs, such as Christmas), audience-cue (a hint about who it suits) or presentation (such as animated or live action). | `TEXT` |
| `synonyms` | JSON array of other words that mean this tag, so a tagger saying lager is read as beer. | `TEXT` |
| `aliases` | JSON array of former slugs of this tag, so clips tagged under an old name still match after a rename. | `TEXT` |
| `updated_at` | When the tag last changed, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

### taxa_closure

Every ancestor and descendant pair in the tag trees, including each tag paired with itself. Rebuilt from taxa whenever the trees change, so "everything under drinks" is one lookup.

**Kept:** Cleared and rebuilt in full from taxa whenever the tag trees change.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ancestor` | The broader tag (taxa.slug). | `TEXT` · key |
| `descendant` | A tag at or below it (taxa.slug). | `TEXT` · key |

### taxonomy_seed_revisions

Which shipped batches of new tags this install has already received. Each batch is applied once, so a tag the operator later deletes is not added back.

**Kept:** Kept forever, so a shipped tag the operator deleted never comes back.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | The shipped tag batch's number. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `applied_at` | When the batch was applied, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_sources

The remote collections clips are downloaded from: archive.org collections and YouTube channels or playlists, added by an operator or offered from Loomarr's shipped list. A row stays until the operator deletes it; switching it off keeps its history.

**Kept:** Kept until an operator deletes the source.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | The source's stable id, separate from its address so re-pointing a source keeps its history. | `TEXT` · key |
| `kind` | The provider, archive (archive.org) or youtube. | `TEXT` |
| `uri` | The archive.org identifier or URL, or the YouTube channel or playlist URL. | `TEXT` |
| `label` | The source's display name; when empty the address is shown instead. | `TEXT` |
| `license` | The licence URL the source declares. Empty means unknown, never public domain. | `TEXT` |
| `last_fetched_at` | When the source last had at least one item queued for download, in Unix seconds; 0 means never. | `INTEGER` |
| `created_at` | When the source was added, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `enabled` | 1 when the source is switched on. A switched-off source is not checked, searched or downloaded from. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `fetch_every_seconds` | How often to check this source for new clips, in seconds. NULL uses the global setting; 0 means never check it automatically. | `INTEGER` · may be empty |
| `fetch_max_per_run` | The most items to download from this source in one check. NULL uses the global setting. | `INTEGER` · may be empty |
| `country` | The country the source serves, as a two-letter ISO code. Empty means it follows the install's own location. | `TEXT` |
| `last_checked_at` | When the last check of the source finished, even if it found nothing new, in Unix seconds; 0 means never. | `INTEGER` |
| `check_failure_count` | How many checks in a row have failed since the last success. Sets how long to wait before retrying. | `INTEGER` |
| `check_retry_at` | Earliest time to retry after a failed check, in Unix seconds; 0 means no wait. | `INTEGER` |
| `check_lease_until` | While a check is running, the time its claim on the source expires, in Unix seconds; 0 means no check is running. | `INTEGER` |
| `scan_cursor` | The provider's id for the last item examined in the sweep in progress, so a check resumes where the previous one stopped. Empty when no sweep is in progress. | `TEXT` |
| `scan_watermark` | The provider's id for the newest item seen by the last completed sweep. | `TEXT` |
| `scan_pending_watermark` | The provider's id for the newest item seen when the sweep in progress began. It becomes scan_watermark when that sweep completes. | `TEXT` |

### filler_providers

One on/off switch per provider. A remote source downloads only when both it and its provider are switched on.

**Kept:** Kept forever; there is one fixed row per provider.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | The provider, archive or youtube. | `TEXT` · key |
| `enabled` | 1 when the provider is switched on. | `BOOLEAN` |

### filler_source_check_outcomes

Counts of what source checks found, per source, for the sweep in progress or the last completed one. Cleared when a new sweep begins; deleted with the source.

**Kept:** Replaced by each new check of the source; goes with its source (deleted when that is).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source_id` | The source checked (filler_sources.id). | `TEXT` · key · → `filler_sources.id` |
| `disposition` | What happened to the items: queued (sent for download), already_known, too_short, too_long, live (a live stream), upcoming (not yet available), private, unavailable or metadata_incomplete. | `TEXT` · key |
| `item_count` | How many items had that outcome. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_pulls

A proposed batch of clips to download, which an operator approves or dismisses. Decided pulls are kept as history of what was agreed to.

**Kept:** Pending pulls are kept. The nightly housekeeping task deletes a dismissed pull 180 days after it was dismissed, and an approved one with its download run.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the pull. | `TEXT` · key |
| `title` | A short summary of what the pull is for. | `TEXT` |
| `reason` | Why Loomarr proposed it, such as the coverage gap it fills. Shown above the plan. | `TEXT` |
| `proposed_by` | Who or what proposed it, such as a user id or a job name. | `TEXT` |
| `status` | pending, approved or dismissed. | `TEXT` |
| `note` | The operator's note narrowing the pull, given at approval. | `TEXT` |
| `plan_json` | JSON document of the plan: what was asked for, the items selected (each with its source, address, estimate and why it was chosen, including any the operator dropped), the candidates turned down and why, and how each source was treated. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the pull was proposed, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `decided_at` | When it was approved or dismissed, in Unix seconds; 0 while pending. | `INTEGER` |
| `decided_by` | Who approved or dismissed it. Empty while pending. | `TEXT` |

### filler_pull_commits

Links an approved pull to the one download run its approval started. Written in the same step as the approval.

**Kept:** One per approved pull; deleted with its download run.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pull_id` | The approved pull (filler_pulls.id). | `TEXT` · key · → `filler_pulls.id` |
| `acquisition_id` | The download run it started (filler_acquisition_runs.id). | `TEXT` · → `filler_acquisition_runs.id` |

### filler_acquisition_runs

One row per download run: a source check, an approved pull or URLs an admin typed in. Shows what was asked for and how the downloads went. Runs left unfinished by a restart are marked as errors.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task deletes a finished run 90 days after it finished once nothing points at it: no downloaded file and no clip pipeline row. A run whose files are kept is kept.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the run. Downloaded files and prepared clips point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `trigger` | What started it: source (a registered source's check), pull (an approved pull) or manual (URLs typed by an admin). scheduled is also allowed. | `TEXT` |
| `source_id` | The registered source every item came from (filler_sources.id). Empty when items came from several sources or none. | `TEXT` |
| `pull_id` | The approved pull that started it (filler_pulls.id). Empty for other triggers. | `TEXT` |
| `status` | queued, running, success or error. | `TEXT` |
| `requested` | How many items were asked for. | `INTEGER` |
| `fetched` | How many files were downloaded. | `INTEGER` |
| `skipped` | How many items were skipped, mostly because they were already downloaded. | `INTEGER` |
| `failed` | How many items failed to download. | `INTEGER` |
| `empty_count` | How many items returned no clips and no error, usually a mistyped id or an empty source. | `INTEGER` |
| `error` | The error that ended the run. Empty when none. | `TEXT` |
| `started_at` | When the run started, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `completed_at` | When the run finished, in Unix seconds; 0 while still going. | `INTEGER` |
| `updated_at` | When the row last changed, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_acquisition_artifacts

One row per file a download produced, tracking it from download to the clip folder to the catalog. Rows that need repair are kept until someone deals with them.

**Kept:** A file with the provider's id is kept on purpose: it is how the fetcher knows it already has that item, one row per item ever downloaded. One without, catalogued into a clip that has since left, is deleted by the nightly housekeeping task after 90 days. Staged, published and repair files are kept.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the downloaded file. | `TEXT` · key |
| `acquisition_id` | The download run that produced it (filler_acquisition_runs.id). | `TEXT` · → `filler_acquisition_runs.id` |
| `source_id` | The registered source it came from (filler_sources.id). Empty for a typed URL. | `TEXT` |
| `provider` | The provider that downloaded it, such as archive or youtube. | `TEXT` |
| `source_url` | The address that was downloaded. | `TEXT` |
| `staging_path` | Where the file was put while it was being checked, relative to the clip folder. Empty when not staged. | `TEXT` |
| `media_path` | Where the media file is published, relative to the clip folder. | `TEXT` |
| `sidecar_path` | The info file downloaded beside the media, relative to the clip folder. Empty when there is none. | `TEXT` |
| `media_sha256` | The SHA-256 hash of the whole file, in hex. | `TEXT` |
| `media_bytes` | The file's size in bytes. | `INTEGER` |
| `clip_hash` | The clip it became (clips.hash). Empty until it is catalogued. | `TEXT` |
| `state` | staged (downloaded, not yet in the clip folder), published (in the clip folder), consumed (catalogued as a clip) or repair (held back for a person to fix). | `TEXT` |
| `repair_reason` | Why the file needs repair. Empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |
| `completed_at` | When the download finished, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `updated_at` | When the row last changed, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `provider_archive_entry` | The line the downloader records so it never downloads this item again. Empty when the provider gives none. | `TEXT` |
| `provider_archive_committed` | 1 once that line has been saved to the downloader's record. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `remote_id` | The provider's id for the item. Empty for older downloads and typed URLs. | `TEXT` |
| `gap` | The channel coverage gap the download was for, such as era:1990-1999. Empty when it was not chosen for a gap. | `TEXT` |

### filler_clip_pipeline

Each clip's preparation: which step it is at, how that step is going, and the clip's outcome (ready, rejected, waiting for review). One row per clip, deleted with the clip.

**Kept:** Kept while the clip exists; removed when the folder scan drops it or it is merged.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_hash` | The clip being prepared (clips.hash). | `TEXT` · key |
| `stage` | The step the clip is at, in order: probe, transcode, split, screen, defects, language, transcribe, vision, finish. | `TEXT` |
| `status` | How the current step is going: queued, running, done, failed (retried after a wait) or skipped (did not apply). | `TEXT` |
| `progress` | Percent done within the current step, 0 to 100. | `INTEGER` |
| `disposition` | The clip's outcome: running, review (waiting for a person), ready, complete (a composite that has been split), rejected (refused by a check) or dismissed (a person said no). | `TEXT` |
| `reject_reason` | Why the clip was rejected, as a code: unprobeable, too_short, no_audio, no_video, black_content, silent_content, too_quiet, unplayable, defect, language, duplicate, screening, sliver or unidentified. Empty when not rejected. | `TEXT` |
| `reject_detail` | The measurement behind the rejection, such as a duration under the minimum or the language heard. | `TEXT` |
| `attempts` | How many times the current step has been tried. Resets when the clip moves on. | `INTEGER` |
| `next_run` | When the row may next be worked on, in Unix seconds; 0 means now. | `INTEGER` |
| `stages_json` | JSON array of the finished steps, each with its status, an explanatory note for a skip or failure, attempts, and start and finish times. | `TEXT` |
| `enrolled_at` | When the clip entered preparation, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `updated_at` | When the row last changed, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `force_run` | 1 when a person asked to re-run the current step, so it runs even if it would normally be skipped. Cleared once the step runs. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `acquisition_id` | The download run that brought the clip in (filler_acquisition_runs.id). Empty for clips dropped into the folder by hand. | `TEXT` |
| `preparation_attempt` | Which attempt at preparing the clip this is, counting from 1. 0 for clips enrolled before this was tracked. | `INTEGER` |
| `preparation_started_at` | When the current preparation attempt began, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `preparation_start_reason` | Why the current attempt began: enrollment (the clip was new) or restart. | `TEXT` |
| `preparation_progress` | Percent done across the whole preparation attempt; -1 means unknown. | `INTEGER` |
| `stage_queued_at` | When the current step was queued, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `stage_started_at` | When the current step started running, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_clip_variants

Pairs of clips that are different versions of the same ad, such as a cut-down or another ending. A break never carries two versions, and airing one rests the others.

**Kept:** Moved to the better copy when a clip is merged. A pair whose clips have both left the catalog is deleted by the nightly housekeeping, unless the catalog is empty (an unmounted drive).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `a_hash` | One clip of the pair (clips.hash); always the smaller hash. | `TEXT` · key |
| `b_hash` | The other clip of the pair (clips.hash). | `TEXT` · key |

### filler_clip_fingerprints

A saved picture-and-sound fingerprint of each clip, used to spot copies and versions of the same ad. Recomputed when the fingerprint method changes; removed when the clip is.

**Kept:** Kept while the clip exists; removed when the folder scan drops it or it is merged.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_hash` | The clip fingerprinted (clips.hash). | `TEXT` · key |
| `algorithm` | The fingerprint method and its version. | `TEXT` · key |
| `fingerprint_json` | JSON document with the clip's duration and the hashes of its sampled video frames and audio. | `TEXT` |

### filler_clip_defects

Each clip's latest picture and sound defect check, against a quality bar set by the clip's era, and the verdict it earned. One row per clip, replaced on each new measurement.

**Kept:** Kept while the clip exists; removed when the folder scan drops it or it is merged.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_hash` | The clip checked (clips.hash). | `TEXT` · key |
| `measurement_version` | The version of the measuring method. Clips measured under an older one are measured again. | `TEXT` |
| `floor_version` | The version of the quality bars the clip was judged against. | `TEXT` |
| `era` | The clip era the verdict was judged against. | `INTEGER` |
| `outcome` | What the detectors decided: pass, fail, borderline (between the bars) or undecided (too little picture to judge). | `TEXT` |
| `readings_json` | JSON document of the raw measurements, such as blockiness, blur, dropouts, interlacing, upscaling and audio clipping. | `TEXT` |
| `assessment_json` | JSON document of the era bar used and each check's outcome, measured value and bar. | `TEXT` |
| `measured_at` | When the clip was measured, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `judgement_json` | JSON document of a vision model's ruling on a borderline clip and its reason. Empty until there is one. | `TEXT` · may be empty |
| `judge_failures` | How many times asking the vision model brought back no ruling since the last one. | `INTEGER` |
| `verdict` | The final standing: pass, fail, undecided (too little picture; allowed to air) or pending (a borderline clip waiting for a ruling). | `TEXT` |
| `verdict_reason` | What decided the verdict, such as the detectors or the judge's reason. | `TEXT` |
| `label` | A maintainer's own pass or fail label for the clip, used to tune the bars. Empty when unlabelled. | `TEXT` |
| `label_era` | The clip era the label was given against; 0 when unlabelled. | `INTEGER` |
| `labelled_at` | When the label was given, in Unix seconds; 0 when unlabelled. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_inferior_copies

Copies of an ad that lost to a better copy of the same ad and were merged into it. Kept so the same file is never catalogued again.

**Kept:** Kept forever, so a copy merged away is never catalogued again.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_hash` | The losing copy's former clip hash. | `TEXT` · key |
| `source_hash` | The hash of the file the losing copy came from, so the same file offered again is skipped. Equal to clip_hash when it was not re-encoded. | `TEXT` |
| `survivor_hash` | The copy it lost to (clips.hash). | `TEXT` |
| `decided_at` | When the copies were merged, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_ready_events

A record written when a clip becomes ready to air, at the same moment it joins the playable catalog. One per clip.

**Kept:** One per clip, kept while the clip exists; the nightly housekeeping task deletes it 30 days after it was written once its clip has left the catalog.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the event, as ready:<clip hash>. | `TEXT` · key |
| `clip_hash` | The clip that became ready (clips.hash). | `TEXT` |
| `acquisition_id` | The download run that brought the clip in (filler_acquisition_runs.id). Empty for clips from a folder. | `TEXT` |
| `enrollment_kind` | What let the clip into filler: acquisition (a download run) or source (a clip folder or source the operator chose). | `TEXT` |
| `enrollment_ref` | The download run id or source id behind enrollment_kind. | `TEXT` |
| `placement` | Where it may be scheduled, break_body or bookend. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the clip became ready, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_curated_offers

Which entries from Loomarr's shipped list of curated sources this install has been offered. An offer adds the source switched off, and the offer is kept after the source is deleted so a deleted source stays deleted.

**Kept:** Kept forever, so a curated source the operator deleted stays deleted.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source_id` | The offered source (filler_sources.id). | `TEXT` · key |
| `list_version` | The version of the shipped list that first offered it. | `TEXT` |
| `offered_at` | When it was offered, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `stations` | Comma-separated station ids the shipped list ties the source to, refreshed on every offer. | `TEXT` |
| `local_state` | What Loomarr did about nearby stations: empty (nothing), on (switched it on for a nearby place), operator (it was already on, so it is left to the operator) or off (the operator switched it back off, so it stays off). | `TEXT` |

### filler_airings

Each time a clip aired on a channel, used to rest clips between airings across the household. Airings from the last eight weeks are kept, plus each clip's newest few beyond that.

**Kept:** Trimmed each time a clip airs to its last eight weeks plus its newest four airings. Once the clip has left the catalog, its airings older than eight weeks are deleted by the nightly housekeeping, unless the catalog is empty (an unmounted drive).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel_id` | The channel it aired on. | `TEXT` · key |
| `clip_hash` | The clip that aired (clips.hash). | `TEXT` · key |
| `aired_at_ms` | When the clip was scheduled to start, in Unix milliseconds. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `recorded_at_ms` | When playout recorded the airing, in Unix milliseconds. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_context_reports

Suggestions about a clip's year, country or station found by researching it online, with the pages cited, plus Loomarr's own uncited era guesses. Only a confident, cited geography finding updates the clip; the rest are shown as suggestions.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task deletes a report once a newer one of the same kind (cited, or a guess) exists for an older revision of the clip, and every report 30 days after it was written once the clip has left the catalog.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_hash` | The clip researched (clips.hash). | `TEXT` · key |
| `producer` | What made the suggestion: the research model (context-model:<name>), or observation for Loomarr's own uncited era guess. | `TEXT` · key |
| `producer_version` | The producer's version; for an observation, what the guess came from (vision or split). | `TEXT` · key |
| `adapter` | The search service used to find pages, such as web. Empty for an observation. | `TEXT` · key |
| `adapter_version` | The search service's version. Empty for an observation. | `TEXT` · key |
| `input_revision` | The clip's enrichment_revision the research was based on. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `report_json` | JSON document of the report: the suggested year or decade, country, scope, station, confidence and explanation, and the search query and pages it cites. | `TEXT` |
| `completed_at` | When the research finished, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

### broadcast_stations

A directory of over-the-air TV stations that filler clips can name, so a clip titled with a station's call sign is placed in that station's town. Shipped with Loomarr and replaced whole at startup when a newer revision ships. Not related to Loomarr's own channels.

**Kept:** Replaced whole at startup whenever a newer shipped directory arrives.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the station. `fcc:` and the FCC facility id, or `wd:` and the Wikidata id for a station only Wikidata knows. | `TEXT` · key |
| `country` | The two-letter country code (US territories have their own, such as PR). | `TEXT` |
| `city` | The station's community of license. | `TEXT` |
| `region` | The state or territory postal code. | `TEXT` |
| `latitude` | Latitude of the community of license. | `REAL` |
| `longitude` | Longitude of the community of license. | `REAL` |

### broadcast_station_call_signs

Every call sign a broadcast station has held, with the dates it was used. Replaced with the station directory.

**Kept:** Replaced with the station directory; goes with its station (deleted when that is).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `station_id` | The station (broadcast_stations.id). | `TEXT` · key · → `broadcast_stations.id` |
| `call_sign` | The base call sign without suffixes such as -TV, for example WEWS. | `TEXT` · key |
| `from_date` | The first day the station used it, as YYYY-MM-DD. Empty when unknown. | `TEXT` · key |
| `to_date` | The day it stopped (not included), as YYYY-MM-DD. Empty when it is still in use or unknown. | `TEXT` |

### broadcast_station_seed_revisions

One row per revision of the shipped station directory that startup has applied. Kept forever.

**Kept:** Kept forever, as the record of which shipped directory revisions were applied.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | The revision number of the shipped station directory. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `applied_at` | When it was applied, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

## How filler clips are checked

Filler clips (vintage ads, promos and bumpers between shows) are examined by AI models and other checks before and after they air. These tables remember each model call and what it cost, the descriptive facts the checks filled in, web-research allowances, and the reel-splitting journals.

### filler_inference_evaluations

One row per model call made about a filler clip, written before the call (as a spend reservation) and updated once the call finishes with what it actually used and cost. Callers include the defect judge (a vision model ruling on borderline picture defects) and the long-reel structure check.

**Kept:** Settled calls are deleted by the nightly housekeeping task after 180 days, once no structure-window call points at them; reserved ones (in flight) are kept. An unused budget hold is removed at once so its retry can take its place.

**The call.** One row is one call to a model; these say which check made it and how it ended.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the call. Spoken-safety events and the structure call journal point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `cache_key` | SHA-256 of every input that could change the answer (clip, role, model, media sizes and all the version columns), so identical retries can be recognised. Run, times and cost are not part of it. | `TEXT` |
| `clip_hash` | The filler clip the call was about (clips.hash). For a long-reel structure check it is the SHA-256 of the reel's source file. | `TEXT` |
| `run_id` | The batch run the call belonged to, used for the per-run spend ceiling. Empty when the call was not part of a run. | `TEXT` |
| `role` | Which check made the call, for example defect_judge or complete_timeline_structure. | `TEXT` |
| `rung` | The step within that check, for example defects or window_video. Empty when the check has no steps. | `TEXT` |
| `state` | Where the call stands. reserved means spend is set aside and the call is under way; completed means it answered; failed means it did not; held_budget means a spend ceiling (per clip, per day or per run) stopped it, or the provider charged more than was reserved. | `TEXT` |
| `latency_ms` | How long the call took, in milliseconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `attempts` | How many times the request was sent to the provider. | `INTEGER` |
| `outcome` | window_complete once a structure-window call has answered; empty for every other call. | `TEXT` |
| `failure_reason` | Why the call did not complete, for example a spend ceiling or a failure class such as transport. Empty on success. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the call was reserved, in Unix seconds. Also decides which day's ceiling it counts against (UTC). | `INTEGER` |
| `updated_at` | When the row last changed (reserved or settled), in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

**Who answered.** One provider and model asked, and one that answered, per call. Comparing them is how a routing service's substitutions show up.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requested_provider` | The AI provider Loomarr asked, such as ollama or openrouter. | `TEXT` |
| `requested_model` | The model Loomarr asked for. | `TEXT` |
| `resolved_provider` | The provider that actually answered, as reported back. Empty until the call settles. | `TEXT` |
| `resolved_model` | The model that actually answered, as reported back. Empty until the call settles. | `TEXT` |
| `upstream_provider` | The provider behind a routing service (such as OpenRouter) that served the call. Empty when not known. | `TEXT` |
| `generation_id` | The provider's own ID for the response, for matching against its billing. Empty when none was given. | `TEXT` |
| `capability_snapshot` | Identity of the model endpoint and its capabilities at the time of the call. | `TEXT` |

**What was sent.** One media excerpt per call; its size is what the cost estimate is worked out from.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `modalities_json` | JSON list of the kinds of input sent, such as text, image, audio or video. | `TEXT` |
| `derivative_bytes` | Size in bytes of the media excerpt sent to the model. 0 when none was sent. | `INTEGER` |
| `derivative_duration_ms` | Length of the media excerpt sent, in milliseconds. 0 when none was sent. | `INTEGER` |
| `derivative_pixels` | Pixel count of the image or frames sent. 0 when none was sent. | `INTEGER` |

**Tokens.** The usage the provider reported for this call, one count per kind, kept to check its bill against.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt_tokens` | Input tokens the provider reported. | `INTEGER` |
| `completion_tokens` | Output tokens the provider reported. | `INTEGER` |
| `reasoning_tokens` | Reasoning tokens the provider reported. | `INTEGER` |
| `cached_tokens` | Input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache. | `INTEGER` |
| `cache_write_tokens` | Input tokens written into the provider's prompt cache. | `INTEGER` |
| `image_tokens` | Tokens the provider counted for images. | `INTEGER` |
| `audio_tokens` | Tokens the provider counted for audio. | `INTEGER` |
| `video_tokens` | Tokens the provider counted for video. | `INTEGER` |

**Cost.** The spend ceilings (per clip, per day, per run) add up reserved_nano_usd across calls in one statement, which needs it on the call's own row.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `charged_amount` | The charge exactly as the provider reported it, as a decimal string. Empty when no charge was reported. | `TEXT` |
| `charged_currency` | Currency of the reported charge, USD when known. Empty when no charge was reported. | `TEXT` |
| `charged_nano_usd` | The reported charge in billionths of a US dollar. 0 when nothing was charged or reported. | `INTEGER` |
| `estimated_nano_usd` | Loomarr's own estimate of the cost, in billionths of a US dollar. | `INTEGER` |
| `reserved_nano_usd` | The amount counted against the spend ceilings, in billionths of a US dollar. It starts as the pre-call reservation and becomes the actual charge when the call settles; a held call counts 0. | `INTEGER` |
| `price_snapshot` | Fingerprint of the provider price list the cost was worked out from. Empty when none was recorded. | `TEXT` |

**Versions.** The cache key hashes every one of these, so an answer is reused only when nothing that shaped it changed; they describe this call and no other.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `evidence_version` | Version of the evidence (measurements or media set) the call was based on. | `TEXT` |
| `extractor_version` | Version of the step that prepared the media excerpt. | `TEXT` |
| `prompt_version` | Version or fingerprint of the prompt sent. | `TEXT` |
| `schema_version` | Version or fingerprint of the answer format the model was asked to follow. | `TEXT` |
| `taxonomy_version` | Version of the vocabulary or bar the answer was judged against. | `TEXT` |
| `admission_policy_version` | Version of the rules that decide what the answer is allowed to unlock. | `TEXT` |
| `role_policy_version` | Version of the check's own rules. | `TEXT` |


### filler_inference_budget_guards

One lock row per spend-ceiling scope. Reserving a model call locks the matching rows first, so two calls cannot both slip under the same ceiling at once. Rows are created on first use and never removed.

**Kept:** Kept forever; there is one small lock row per spend-ceiling scope.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scope` | The ceiling being guarded, written as clip:<clip hash>, day:<YYYY-MM-DD in UTC> or run:<run id>. | `TEXT` · key |

### filler_enrichment_axes

The accepted answer for one descriptive fact ("axis") about one filler clip, such as its era, brand or role, with where the answer came from. A stronger or more confident answer replaces a weaker one; no row means the fact is still unknown. Rows follow the clip if its identity changes.

**Kept:** Kept while the clip exists. Once it has left the catalog, rows not updated for 30 days are deleted by the nightly housekeeping, unless the catalog is empty (an unmounted drive).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_hash` | The filler clip described (clips.hash). | `TEXT` · key |
| `axis` | Which fact. role (commercial, bumper, station_id, psa, trailer, interstitial, political or news), era, audience, brand, geography, language, product, format, seasonal, audience-cue or presentation. | `TEXT` · key |
| `state` | complete means the answer stands (an empty value is an honest "checked, none applies"); unsupported means the producer withdrew or has no answer; stale means the answer may be refreshed by a new result of the same strength. | `TEXT` |
| `value_json` | The answer as JSON, using one of text, year, tags (taxonomy slugs) or geography (scope, country, network, station, airDate), depending on the axis. | `TEXT` |
| `evidence_kind` | Where the answer came from, weakest to strongest: inference (a model's guess), source_default (the source's usual value), trusted_mapping, content_observation (seen or heard in the clip), item_metadata (the item's own listing) or operator (an admin's edit). | `TEXT` |
| `evidence_rank` | The strength of evidence_kind as a number, 1 (inference) to 6 (operator). | `INTEGER` |
| `evidence_reference` | What the answer was based on, such as the source listing or the admin screen an edit came through. | `TEXT` |
| `confidence` | How sure the producer was, from 0 to 100. Operator edits are 100. | `INTEGER` |
| `producer` | The pass that gave the answer, for example deterministic-metadata, a text-model pass or operator. | `TEXT` |
| `producer_version` | Version of that producer's rules or prompt. | `TEXT` |
| `taxonomy_version` | Version of the tag vocabulary the answer was checked against. Empty when the axis does not use tags. | `TEXT` |
| `observed_at` | When the producer made the observation, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `updated_at` | When this answer was accepted into the row, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_enrichment_passes

Marks that one enrichment producer, at one version, has finished with one clip. It is what stops the same work (and its model spend) being repeated; a clip is picked again when the producer version or taxonomy changes, or, for free passes, when the clip's descriptive inputs change.

**Kept:** Kept while the clip exists (they stop a paid pass from running twice). The nightly housekeeping task deletes a pass 30 days after it ran once its clip has left the catalog.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_hash` | The filler clip the pass ran on (clips.hash). | `TEXT` · key |
| `producer` | The pass that ran, for example deterministic-metadata or a text-model pass. | `TEXT` · key |
| `producer_version` | Version of that pass's rules or prompt. | `TEXT` · key |
| `taxonomy_version` | Version of the tag vocabulary the pass used. Empty when it used none. | `TEXT` · key |
| `completed_at` | When the pass finished, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `input_revision` | The clip's enrichment revision (clips.enrichment_revision) the pass saw. When the clip's revision moves past it, free passes run again. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_research_web_attempts

One row per web search made to research a filler clip, so the same clip at the same description revision is never searched twice with the same search setup. Rows go when the clip is deleted.

**Kept:** Goes with its clip (deleted when that is).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_hash` | The filler clip researched (clips.hash). | `TEXT` · key · → `clips.hash` |
| `input_revision` | The clip's enrichment revision the search was made for. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `adapter_version` | Identity of the web-search setup used, including the provider (and, for SearXNG, a short fingerprint of its address). | `TEXT` · key |
| `provider` | The web-search provider. brave (Brave Search) or searxng (a SearXNG server). | `TEXT` |
| `reserved_at` | When the search was booked, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_research_web_usage

One row per calendar month counting web searches against the monthly limit set in settings. Searches are refused once the count reaches the limit.

**Kept:** The last 12 months; the nightly housekeeping task deletes older ones.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `month` | The month counted, as YYYY-MM in UTC. | `TEXT` · key |
| `request_count` | Web searches made that month, including an admin's connection test. | `INTEGER` |
| `last_provider` | The provider used for the most recent search, brave or searxng. Empty before the first. | `TEXT` |
| `last_success_at` | When a search last succeeded that month, in Unix seconds. 0 means none yet. | `INTEGER` |
| `last_failure_at` | When a search last failed that month, in Unix seconds. 0 means none yet. A failure newer than the last success shows web search as degraded. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_structure_window_call_ledger

One row per model call in the long-reel structure check, which sends a reel to a video model in windows to find where each separate clip starts and ends. The row is booked before the call and completed with the answer; a call that got no answer is retried as a new attempt.

**Kept:** Settled calls are deleted by the nightly housekeeping task after 180 days; open and budget-held ones are kept. An attempt held back by the spend ceiling is replaced by its retry.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `request_sha256` | SHA-256 of the exact request. With attempt, identifies the row. | `TEXT` · key |
| `attempt` | Which try of this request, from 1. A retry after a lost answer adds the next attempt; a retry after a budget hold replaces the held row. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `evaluation_id` | The matching cost record (filler_inference_evaluations.id). | `TEXT` · → `filler_inference_evaluations.id` |
| `source_sha256` | SHA-256 of the reel's source file. | `TEXT` |
| `media_set_sha256` | SHA-256 of the full set of windows planned for the reel. | `TEXT` |
| `window_ordinal` | Which window of the reel this call covers, from 0. | `INTEGER` |
| `assessor_id` | Identity of the model setup that assessed the window. | `TEXT` |
| `state` | open means the call is booked and has no answer yet; held_budget means a spend ceiling stopped it; settled means the outcome is recorded. | `TEXT` |
| `reservation_json` | The full booked request as JSON, including the media set, window, model, prompt and schema fingerprints, and the spend requested. | `TEXT` |
| `record_sha256` | SHA-256 of the settled record. Empty until settled. | `TEXT` |
| `record_json` | The settled record as JSON, including the model that answered, tokens, charge, result state (accepted, failed, unsettled, held_budget or over_reservation) and fingerprints of the response. Empty until settled. | `TEXT` · may be empty |
| `requested_at` | When the call was booked, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `assessed_at` | When the answer was recorded, in Unix seconds. 0 until settled. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_split_proposals

A proposed cut list for a compilation reel waiting for an admin's review, one per reel. Confirming it turns the segments into separate clips and removes the proposal; dismissing it also removes it, and it goes when the reel leaves the catalog.

**Kept:** Kept until an admin confirms or dismisses it, or its reel leaves the catalog.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the proposal. | `TEXT` · key |
| `clip_hash` | The compilation reel being split (clips.hash). | `TEXT` |
| `segments_json` | JSON list of proposed segments, each with its index, start and end in milliseconds, proposed name and where the name came from, and suggested era, audience and tags. The admin's edits are saved here. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the proposal was made, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |
| `claim_token` | A lock held while a confirm is publishing the segments, so two confirms cannot run at once. Empty when unlocked. | `TEXT` |
| `claim_expires_at` | When the lock lapses if not renewed, in Unix seconds. 0 when unlocked. | `INTEGER` |

### filler_split_shadow_decisions

A side-by-side record, made while a new splitting rule is being trialled, of what the current rule and the new certified rule would each do with one split proposal. Kept after the proposal itself is gone; rows are never changed.

**Kept:** Kept while the proposal exists; once it is gone, the nightly housekeeping task deletes the decision 180 days after it was made.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the decision, derived from its content. | `TEXT` · key |
| `proposal_id` | The split proposal it was made for (filler_split_proposals.id). The proposal may since have been removed. | `TEXT` |
| `clip_hash` | The compilation reel (clips.hash). | `TEXT` |
| `source_sha256` | SHA-256 of the reel's source file. Empty when not known. | `TEXT` |
| `assessment_sha256` | SHA-256 of the structure assessment the new rule used. Empty when there was none. | `TEXT` |
| `policy_version` | Version of the splitting policy compared. | `TEXT` |
| `decision_json` | The full decision as JSON. For each rule (legacy and certified) it holds a verdict and the spans it would confirm, hold (with a reason) or discard. | `TEXT` |
| `observed_at` | When the comparison was made, in Unix seconds. | `INTEGER` |

## Notifications

Messages Loomarr sends outside the app (email, chat services, push apps, Browser Push) and where they go. A notification is recorded once, then sent to each matching destination, with every send attempt kept as a record. Message bodies and plaintext secrets are never stored here.

### notification_destinations

One row per place notifications can be sent, such as a Discord webhook, an ntfy topic or one person's browser for Browser Push. Admins set up household-wide destinations; a person can add their own. A row lasts until it is deleted.

**Kept:** Kept until an admin, or the person who added it, deletes it.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the destination. Delivery attempts refer to it by this id. | `TEXT` · key |
| `means` | The kind of service it sends through. One of email, webhook, discord, ntfy, gotify, apprise, pushover, telegram, mattermost, matrix, web_push (Browser Push), mqtt or slack. | `TEXT` |
| `label` | The name shown for the destination, also shown in delivery history in place of its address. | `TEXT` |
| `scope` | installation for a destination an admin set up for the whole household; person for one that belongs to a single person. | `TEXT` |
| `owner_id` | The person a person-scoped destination belongs to, from users. Empty for installation scope. | `TEXT` |
| `audience` | Who the destination is for. person means its owner's own notifications; approvers means the admins who review requests; operators means the admins who look after the server and library. | `TEXT` |
| `topics_json` | A JSON list of the notification topics the destination receives (the same values as notification_intents.topic). Topics not in the list are never sent here. | `TEXT` |
| `enabled` | 1 when the destination is switched on. A disabled destination receives nothing. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `configuration_json` | A JSON object of the destination's non-secret settings, such as a server address or topic name. | `TEXT` |
| `credentials_encrypted` | The destination's secret settings (tokens, passwords, webhook URLs, push keys), encrypted with Loomarr's encryption key. Unreadable without that key. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the destination was added, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_at` | When the destination was last changed, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `credential_keys_json` | A JSON list naming which secret settings are filled in, without their values, so the app can show them as set without decrypting. NULL for rows made before this was recorded. | `TEXT` · may be empty |
| `subscription_fingerprint` | For Browser Push, a one-way hash of the browser's push address, so one browser is subscribed only once per person. The address can't be recovered from it. Empty for other kinds. | `TEXT` |

### notification_intents

One row per notification Loomarr decided to send, such as "your request was approved" or "a media folder went offline". Its delivery attempts hang off it. Deleted, with its attempts, 30 days after its last attempt finished.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task deletes a notification 30 days after its last attempt finished; ones still sending are kept.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the notification. notification_delivery_attempts point here. | `TEXT` · key |
| `topic` | What happened. account_invitation (an invitation email); local_password_recovery (a password-reset email); proposal_submitted, proposal_approved, proposal_denied (a request was made, approved or denied); acquisition_available, acquisition_gave_up (a requested title arrived, or Loomarr stopped trying); channel_live, channel_degraded (a channel went on air or stopped playing properly); delivery_test (a test sent from a destination's settings); library_folder_offline, library_folder_back (a media folder stopped or started opening again); library_changes_degraded (an arr can no longer report new files); library_needs_you (titles in the library need a person's help). | `TEXT` |
| `recipient_kind` | Who it is for. invitation means the address on a pending invitation; person means one person; approvers means the admins who review requests; operators means the admins who look after the server. | `TEXT` |
| `recipient_id` | The invitation's id, the person's id, or the literal word approvers or operators. For a delivery test, the destination's id. | `TEXT` |
| `reference_kind` | The kind of thing it is about. One of invitation, recovery (a password-recovery request), proposal (a request), title, channel, destination or library (a media folder or arr). | `TEXT` |
| `reference_id` | The id of the thing it is about, in the table that reference_kind names. | `TEXT` |
| `recipient_policy` | mandatory_account for account and security email that always goes out; configurable for everything else, which only reaches destinations that chose the topic. | `TEXT` |
| `template_json` | A JSON object with the few names the message needs (the recipient's name, the subject's name, a short summary), captured when it happened. Never the rendered message or any link secret. | `TEXT` |
| `idempotency_key` | A unique key built from the event and recipient, so the same event never makes two notifications for the same recipient. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the notification was recorded, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `terminal_at` | When its last delivery attempt finished, in Unix seconds. 0 while any attempt is still queued or sending. | `BIGINT` |

### notification_delivery_attempts

One row per try at sending a notification to one destination. A failure that may succeed later queues a new row for the next try, up to 5 tries. Deleted with its notification.

**Kept:** Goes with its notification (deleted when that is).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the attempt. | `TEXT` · key |
| `intent_id` | The notification being sent, from notification_intents. | `TEXT` · → `notification_intents.id` |
| `means` | The kind of service used, with the same values as notification_destinations.means. | `TEXT` |
| `destination_ref` | Which destination it went to. A notification_destinations id, or for account email, invitation: or person: followed by that id. Never the address itself. | `TEXT` |
| `destination_redacted` | A safe name for the destination to show in delivery history, such as its label. Never the address or a secret. | `TEXT` |
| `status` | queued waiting to be sent; sending while a worker has it; delivered when the service accepted it; failed when it didn't go through; suppressed when it was deliberately not sent (destination off or gone, or the person turned the topic off). | `TEXT` |
| `attempt_number` | Which try this is, from 1 to 5. | `INTEGER` |
| `available_at` | When the attempt may be sent, in Unix seconds. Later for retries, which wait before trying again. | `BIGINT` |
| `lease_owner` | Which worker is sending it. Empty unless status is sending. | `TEXT` |
| `lease_expires_at` | When the worker's hold runs out, in Unix seconds. An attempt still sending after this is closed as failed with an unknown outcome. 0 unless sending. | `BIGINT` |
| `started_at` | When a worker started sending it, in Unix seconds. 0 if never started. | `BIGINT` |
| `finished_at` | When it was delivered, failed or suppressed, in Unix seconds. 0 while queued or sending. | `BIGINT` |
| `provider_message_id` | The id the service gave the sent message, when it gave one. Empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |
| `failure_class` | Why a failed attempt failed. transient_pre_acceptance (a temporary problem before the service took it, so it is retried); permanent (won't work if tried again); ambiguous_acceptance (the service may or may not have taken it, so it is not retried); cancelled. Empty unless failed. | `TEXT` |
| `outcome_code` | What went wrong, in terms an admin can act on. delivery_disabled, destination_unavailable, preference_disabled (reasons for suppressing); means_unavailable, recipient_rejected, configuration_invalid, transport_unavailable, acceptance_ambiguous, cancelled, worker_interrupted (reasons for failing). Empty when delivered or still in progress. | `TEXT` |
| `created_at` | When the attempt was queued, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |

### title_requesters

One row per person who asked for a title, recorded when an admin approves their request, so later news about it (the title arrived) reaches them.

**Kept:** Goes with the title or the person.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title_key` | The title asked for (a titles key). | `TEXT` · key · → `titles.key` |
| `person_id` | The person who asked for it, from users. | `TEXT` · key · → `users.id` |
| `created_at` | When their request was approved, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |

### channel_requesters

One row per person who asked for a channel, recorded when an admin approves their request, so later news about it (the channel went live) reaches them.

**Kept:** Goes with the channel or the person.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel_id` | The channel asked for (a channels id). | `TEXT` · key · → `channels.id` |
| `person_id` | The person who asked for it, from users. | `TEXT` · key · → `users.id` |
| `created_at` | When their request was approved, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |

## Settings and housekeeping

How this installation is configured and what it remembers about its own running: saved settings and the keys that encrypt their secrets, background tasks, the Dashboard's recent activity, and the Diagnostics and crash-report logs that are cleaned up on a schedule.

### settings

One saved setting value. Every setting resolves environment variable, then this table, then the built-in default, so a key with no row uses its default. A row is created when someone saves the setting (or Loomarr records internal state such as its instance id) and deleted when it is reset.

**Kept:** Kept until the setting is reset to its default.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | The setting's name, such as activity.retention, as listed in the configuration reference. A few keys hold Loomarr's own state, such as instance_id. | `TEXT` · key |
| `value` | The stored value as text. Secret settings (API keys, tokens) are stored encrypted, beginning with loomarr-secret:v1:, and can only be read with the installation key. | `TEXT` |
| `updated_at` | When the value was last written, in Unix seconds. 0 means unknown (written before this was tracked). | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_by` | The id of the person who last changed it, pointing at users. Empty for values Loomarr wrote itself. | `TEXT` · may be empty |
| `env_override` | 1 when an admin has taken the setting back from its environment variable, so the saved value wins even while the variable is still set. 0 means a set environment variable wins. | `BOOLEAN` |

### secret_protection_metadata

A single row that records which installation key encrypts this database's secrets. The key itself is never stored here; it comes from LOOMARR_ENCRYPTION_KEY or the encryption.key file. Loomarr refuses to start if the supplied key doesn't match.

**Kept:** Kept forever: a single row Loomarr checks the installation key against at startup.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `singleton` | Always 1; the table holds at most one row. | `INTEGER` · key |
| `installation_key_fingerprint` | A non-secret fingerprint of the installation key (sha256: followed by the start of its hash), used to detect the wrong key. Updated when the installation key is replaced. | `TEXT` |

### secret_data_keys

The data-encryption keys that encrypt secret settings and other stored credentials, each kept encrypted by the installation key. Rotating the key (Security settings) adds a new active key; older keys are kept forever so values they encrypted can still be read.

**Kept:** Kept forever: one row per key rotation, so values encrypted with an older key can still be read.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the key. Each encrypted value names the key that sealed it. | `TEXT` · key |
| `wrapped_key` | The data key, encrypted with the installation key (begins with loomarr-dek:v1:). | `TEXT` |
| `active` | 1 for the one key used to encrypt new secrets; 0 for retired keys kept for reading. | `BOOLEAN` |
| `created_at` | When the key was created, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |

### scheduled_jobs

The running state of one recurring background task shown on the Tasks page. Which tasks exist and when they run come from the code and the job schedule settings; a row is created the first time a task is seen and kept forever, even if the task later disappears from the code.

**Kept:** Kept forever: one row per background task, kept even after a task is removed from Loomarr.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | The task's name, such as housekeeping. | `TEXT` · key |
| `last_run` | When the task last started, in Unix seconds. 0 means it has never run. | `BIGINT` |
| `last_result` | How the last run ended. ok means it succeeded, error means it failed, empty means it hasn't run yet. | `TEXT` |
| `last_error` | The error message from the last run, or empty if it succeeded. | `TEXT` |
| `next_run` | When the task is next due, in Unix seconds. Advanced when a run is claimed, so the same run doesn't start twice. | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_at` | When the row was last written, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `paused` | 1 when an admin has paused the task, so it no longer runs on its schedule until resumed. | `BOOLEAN` |

### interactive_operations

Progress of one long action someone started in the app (downloading an AI model, or detecting where a filler reel should be split), so the page can pick it up again after a reconnect. Anything still queued or running when Loomarr restarts is marked as an error.

**Kept:** Finished ones are deleted by the nightly housekeeping task 7 days after they finish; queued and running ones are kept.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the operation; the app polls it by this id. | `TEXT` · key |
| `kind` | What the operation is. llm_pull downloads an AI model; filler_split detects split points in a filler clip. | `TEXT` |
| `subject` | What it acts on. The model name for llm_pull, the filler clip's id for filler_split. | `TEXT` |
| `status` | queued (accepted, not started), running, success, or error. | `TEXT` |
| `percent` | How far along it is, 0 to 100. For a model download, -1 means the size isn't known yet. | `INTEGER` |
| `completed` | For a model download, bytes downloaded so far of the current layer. 0 otherwise. | `BIGINT` |
| `total` | For a model download, total bytes of the current layer. 0 otherwise. | `BIGINT` |
| `result_id` | For filler_split, the id of the split proposal it produced. Empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |
| `error` | Why it failed, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `started_at` | When it was started, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `completed_at` | When it finished, in Unix seconds. 0 while it is still queued or running. | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_at` | When its progress was last saved, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |

### activity

One line in the Dashboard's Recent activity feed, written when something notable happens, such as a title arriving or a channel changing. Purged by the nightly housekeeping task once older than the activity.retention setting (30 days by default).

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task deletes lines older than activity.retention (30 days by default).

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the entry. | `TEXT` · key |
| `at` | When it happened, in Unix seconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `kind` | Which part of Loomarr wrote it: title, channel, proposal (a suggested lineup), or system. | `TEXT` |
| `level` | How serious it is, which sets the coloured dot. info, warn, or error. | `TEXT` |
| `text` | The sentence shown in the feed. | `TEXT` |
| `subject_id` | The id of the channel, title or proposal it concerns, or empty. | `TEXT` |

### diagnostic_events

One technical event recorded for Diagnostics, from the server's own logs or reported by the web, TV and phone apps. The nightly housekeeping task deletes events older than the diagnostics.retention setting (7 days by default), then the oldest ones while the total exceeds diagnostics.max_storage_mb (512 MiB by default).

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task deletes events older than diagnostics.retention (7 days by default), then the oldest while over diagnostics.max_storage_mb.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the event. | `TEXT` · key |
| `occurred_at_ms` | When it happened, in Unix milliseconds (by the sender's clock for app events). | `BIGINT` |
| `received_at_ms` | When the server recorded it, in Unix milliseconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `level` | How serious it is. debug, info, warn, or error. | `TEXT` |
| `source` | Which program observed it. server, web, android_tv, apple_tv, ios, or android. | `TEXT` |
| `subsystem` | The part of Loomarr it came from, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `event` | The event's name, such as player.media_error for an app playback error. | `TEXT` |
| `message` | The human-readable message, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `request_id` | The API request it belongs to, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `playback_session_id` | The app playback session it belongs to, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `channel_id` | The channel it concerns, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `schedule_block_id` | The schedule block it concerns, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `job_id` | The background job it belongs to, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `process_run_id` | The process run it belongs to, pointing at diagnostic_process_runs, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `actor_id` | Who caused it, usually a user id. App events sent with an API token say api_token. Empty when no one is involved. | `TEXT` |
| `instance_id` | Which Loomarr server recorded it, when known. | `TEXT` |
| `attributes_json` | Extra details as a JSON object of named values (secrets removed before storage), such as the app version and platform for app events. | `TEXT` |
| `size_bytes` | The event's estimated size, counted toward the Diagnostics storage budget. | `BIGINT` |

### diagnostic_process_runs

One run of an external media program, usually ffmpeg (playout, filler transcodes, encoder probes), with its outcome. Its output is kept in a file under the diagnostics folder. The nightly housekeeping task deletes finished runs, and their output files, once they ended longer ago than diagnostics.retention (7 days by default), then the oldest finished ones while Diagnostics is over its storage budget. Runs still going are never deleted.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task deletes finished runs older than diagnostics.retention (7 days by default), then the oldest while over the storage budget; running ones are kept.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the run. | `TEXT` · key |
| `purpose` | What the program was run for, such as playout_program, filler_transcode or capacity_probe. | `TEXT` |
| `parent_run_id` | The run that started this one, pointing at another row here, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `instance_id` | Which Loomarr server ran it. | `TEXT` |
| `channel_id` | The channel it was working for, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `target` | What it was working on, such as an encoder name or output profile, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `schedule_block_id` | The schedule block it was playing, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `job_id` | The background job it belongs to, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `executable` | The program that ran. | `TEXT` |
| `executable_version` | The program's reported version, or empty if not detected. | `TEXT` |
| `command_summary` | The command line it was run with, shortened and with secrets removed. | `TEXT` |
| `started_at_ms` | When it started, in Unix milliseconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `ended_at_ms` | When it ended, in Unix milliseconds. 0 while it is still running. | `BIGINT` |
| `status` | running, succeeded, failed, cancelled, or interrupted (Loomarr stopped before recording how it ended, so the outcome is unknown). | `TEXT` |
| `exit_code` | The program's exit code when it failed with one; empty otherwise. | `INTEGER` · may be empty |
| `termination_reason` | Why the run ended or was stopped, when Loomarr knows, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `first_error` | The first line the program printed, or the error if it printed nothing. | `TEXT` |
| `last_error` | The last line the program printed, or the error it failed with. | `TEXT` |
| `output_ref` | The name of its output file in the diagnostics folder, or empty if output wasn't saved. | `TEXT` |
| `output_bytes` | The size of the output file, in bytes. | `BIGINT` |
| `discarded_lines` | How many output lines were dropped to keep the output file within its size cap. | `BIGINT` |
| `updated_at_ms` | When the row was last updated, in Unix milliseconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `size_bytes` | The run's estimated size including its output file, counted toward the Diagnostics storage budget. | `BIGINT` |

### diagnostic_retained_bytes

Running totals of how much Diagnostics is keeping, updated with every insert and delete so the storage budget can be checked without adding up the big tables. There are two rows, and they are never deleted.

**Kept:** Kept forever: just two running-total rows.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scope` | Which table the total covers. events for diagnostic_events, process_runs for diagnostic_process_runs. | `TEXT` · key |
| `bytes` | The sum of size_bytes across that table. | `BIGINT` |

### client_crash_reports

One crash report sent by the Loomarr TV or phone app, cleaned of secrets before storage. The nightly housekeeping task deletes reports older than 30 days and keeps at most the newest 1,000.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task deletes reports older than 30 days and keeps at most the newest 1,000.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the report. | `TEXT` · key |
| `received_at_ms` | When the server received it, in Unix milliseconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `occurred_at_ms` | When the crash happened by the device's clock, in Unix milliseconds. | `BIGINT` |
| `user_id` | The person signed in on the app that sent it, pointing at users. Empty if unknown or the person has been deleted. | `TEXT` · may be empty · → `users.id` |
| `device_id` | The paired device that sent it, matching device_tokens.token_hash. Empty when not sent from a paired device. | `TEXT` |
| `device_name` | The paired device's name at the time, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `kind` | What crashed. js-fatal is an app error that closed the app, js-error is an app error that was caught, native is a crash of the app's native code. | `TEXT` |
| `platform` | Which app sent it. ios, android, tvos (Apple TV), or android-tv. | `TEXT` |
| `app_version` | The app's version. | `TEXT` |
| `app_build` | The app's build number. | `TEXT` |
| `os_version` | The device's operating system version. | `TEXT` |
| `device_model` | The device's model. | `TEXT` |
| `message` | The error message. | `TEXT` |
| `stack` | The stack trace, or empty. | `TEXT` |
| `breadcrumbs_json` | A JSON list of up to 50 things the app did just before the crash, each with a time, a category (navigation, http, lifecycle or log) and a short message. | `TEXT` |
| `native_payload` | For native crashes, the crash report from Apple's MetricKit as JSON. Empty otherwise. | `TEXT` |

### database_table_rows

How many rows each table held, counted once a day by the nightly housekeeping task after its clean-up. A table whose count only ever rises is one that nothing trims; "Which tables are growing" near the top of this page shows how to compare the latest count with a month ago.

**Kept:** The nightly housekeeping task forgets counts older than 400 days.

| Column | What it holds | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `recorded_at` | The day counted, as the Unix time in seconds of that day's midnight (UTC). | `INTEGER` · key |
| `table_name` | The table counted. Every table except goose_db_version and this one. | `TEXT` · key |
| `row_count` | How many rows the table held after that night's clean-up. | `INTEGER` |

## Tables other libraries own

These come from the tools Loomarr is built on, which document them. Leave them alone.

- `goose_db_version`: which database migrations have run ([goose](https://github.com/pressly/goose)).
